title: Architect, Technology I
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
The Architect, Technology I owns the architecture of the enterprise cloud data platform and leads a team of developers, working with limited supervision. The role also directs a very large offshore team across multiple time zones, setting technical direction, standards, and roadmaps so work stays consistent at scale. The architect applies advanced technical knowledge to complex assignments, independently leads technical components of larger initiatives, and supports business growth and technology integration in a regulated environment.
Responsibilities:
Perform technical and analytical tasks using established methods and tools; apply judgment to adapt approaches for less-routine problems, document methods and results, and escalate novel or ambiguous issues with suggested next steps.
Lead and mentor a team of developers, and direct a large offshore team, setting priorities, coordinating handoffs across time zones, and holding delivery to quality and architecture standards.
Review design artifacts and enforce standards through peer reviews, architecture principles, and documented compliance evidence. Support governance and compliance tracking by maintaining architecture repositories, updating standards documentation, and coordinating audit preparations.
Collaborate with development, infrastructure, and security teams on implementation by providing architecture guidance, reviewing technical designs, and validating integration points.
Define and evolve data platform architecture, including Lakehouse, data mesh and data fabric patterns, event-driven designs, and batch and real-time processing.
Establish data contracts, data quality, observability, lineage, and metadata practices for reusable data products and platform services.
Design for scalability, reliability, performance, disaster recovery, security, and cost optimization.
Identify automation and process improvements by evaluating tooling options, implementing validation scripts, and streamlining documentation workflows.
Maintain architecture documentation and guidelines by updating models, capturing design decisions, and keeping them accessible to project teams.
Deliver reliable outputs for assigned and moderately complex projects; ensure acceptance criteria and compliance requirements are met, document methods, validations, and key assumptions, and keep project leads, stakeholders, and leadership informed of progress and issues.
Required:
Bachelor’s Degree 7 years of experience, or Master’s Degree 6 years of experience, or PhD 2 years of experience.
Significant hands-on experience building and operationalizing enterprise-scale cloud big data platforms.
Strong knowledge of modern data engineering architectures, including cloud-native data platforms, Lakehouse architecture, data mesh and data fabric concepts, event driven architectures, and batch and real-time data processing.
Familiarity with open table formats and interoperable data ecosystems, such as Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, or Apache Hudi.
Experience building reliable data pipelines, data products, and reusable platform services.
Knowledge of data quality, observability, lineage, metadata management, and data governance.
Experience defining and implementing data contracts covering schemas, semantics, quality expectations, ownership, and access policies.
Understanding of data security, privacy, identity and access management, encryption, regulatory requirements, and responsible data use.
Experience designing for scalability, reliability, performance, disaster recovery, and cost optimization.
Familiarity with modern data development and orchestration tools, such as dbt, Airflow, Dagster, Prefect, or comparable technologies.
Experience with serverless architectures including Kubernetes, AWS EKS, and AWS Fargate.
Ability to mentor engineers and influence technical direction across teams.
Demonstrated ability to mentor technical staff, lead cross-functional teams, and drive initiatives to completion.
Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
Ability to operate with high autonomy and minimal supervision, proactively managing stakeholder expectations and keeping leadership informed through clear, concise verbal and written communication.
Preferred
Exposure to or experience with Cloudera Data Platform or another legacy big-data environment (a significant plus).
Experience in the pharmaceutical industry or other highly regulated environments.
Experience working with international development teams across multiple time zones.
Exposure to graph databases and GraphQL.

title: Associate Director, Business Process Owner
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
Purpose
Own the end-to-end governance, health, and continuous improvement of assigned clinical business processes, ensuring processes are inspection-ready, scalable, and aligned to enterprise priorities and regulatory expectations. Partner across Clinical Development Operations and enabling functions to translate strategy into clear process outcomes, drive adoption through change management and learning alignment, and monitor process performance signals to proactively address risk and improve execution. Role may be filled as a Sr. BPO depending on experience and process areas.
Responsibilities
Serve as the accountable owner for assigned clinical business processes across their lifecycle (Engage → Evaluate → Execute → Measure → Sustain), defining process scope, intended outcomes, and decision rights.
Establish and maintain an end-to-end process governance model (standards, forums, escalations, and stakeholder alignment) to ensure consistent global execution and a unified, single voice to the business.
Own process health and sustainability by defining and monitoring key process signals/metrics, identifying emerging issues and risks, and driving timely mitigation and continuous improvement.
Translate business and regulatory needs into clear process requirements and partner with Process Excellence roles (e.g., process design/engineering) to ensure documentation is complete, consistent, and inspection-ready.
Act as the authoritative point of contact for process questions within the domain; curate and maintain process knowledge content and ensure availability of fit-for-purpose guidance for end users.
Lead cross-functional stakeholder engagement to align priorities, trade-offs, and adoption plans, ensuring the right SMEs are engaged at the right time and decisions are transparent and durable.
Partner with stakeholders to ensure change narratives, communications, and role-based training enable effective adoption and sustained performance.
Coordinate and coach a domain SME network to support process adherence, identify improvement opportunities, and reinforce standard ways of working.
Partner with system and business owners to ensure process-to-system alignment, impact assessment for changes, and effective implementation support (e.g., acceptance criteria, UAT input, and readiness planning).
Embed innovation and digital/AI enablement into process oversight and improvements where appropriate, ensuring changes are controlled, compliant, and measurable.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree strongly preferred (e.g., life sciences, engineering, or related discipline).
Minimum of 8 years clinical process management experience required with demonstrated experience owning and governing end-to-end business processes in a regulated environment (clinical development, GxP, quality systems, or similar).
Strong understanding of clinical development operations and the regulatory/inspection context; ability to apply this knowledge to process decisions and risk management.
Proven ability to lead cross-functional alignment and stakeholder management, including conflict resolution and escalation when needed.
Experience defining process performance measures, monitoring process health, and driving continuous improvement using data and structured problem solving.
Familiarity with process design/documentation standards and methods (e.g., process mapping/BPMN, Lean/Six Sigma concepts), including partnering effectively with process architects/engineers.
Experience partnering with technology/system owners on process-to-system alignment and change impacts (requirements, readiness, and UAT support).
Strong change leadership skills, including partnering on communications, training alignment, and adoption/sustainment planning.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to translate complex process topics into clear guidance for diverse audiences.
Ability to work effectively in a matrixed, global environment and manage multiple priorities with sound judgment and accountability.

description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
​​​​​​​ Purpose:
The Change Management & Enablement Associate Director plays a critical role in driving Finance Transformation programs forward as part of enterprise-wide culture and behavior change to enable sustainable adoption of new processes, ways of working, and operating models within AbbVie Finance.  This role goes beyond project delivery to focus on embedding change into the organization’s DNA, ensuring that employees not only adopt new tools and processes, but also embrace the mindsets, behaviors, and cultural shifts required to sustain transformation.
The individual will lead the design and execution of integrated change strategies that influence leadership alignment, employee engagement, and process adoption, ultimately accelerating value realization and long-term organizational effectiveness.
Responsibilities:
Culture & Behavior Change Leadership
Lead Finance Transformation initiatives that drive mindset and behavior change, reinforcing a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and adaptability.
Partner with senior leaders to model and reinforce desired cultural attributes and ways of working.
Work with SMEs to translate transformation objectives into clear behavioral expectations and adoption milestones.
Process & Adoption Transformation
Drive end-to-end adoption of new processes and operating models, ensuring alignment across people, process, and technology.
Identify and address barriers to adoption, focusing on sustainable behavior change vs. one-time implementation.
Embed change into business routines, governance forums, and performance management where appropriate.
Integrated Change Strategy & Execution
Develop and execute holistic change strategies that integrate communications, training, stakeholder engagement, and reinforcement mechanisms.
Apply structured change management methodologies to support both large-scale transformations and targeted process improvements.
Ensure alignment of change activities across cross-functional teams and initiatives.
Stakeholder Engagement & Leadership Alignment
Build strong, trusted partnerships with senior leaders and project teams to drive alignment, sponsorship, and accountability.
Conduct stakeholder and readiness assessments to inform targeted interventions.
Act as a strategic advisor to leaders on navigating organizational change and resistance.
Measurement & Continuous Improvement
Define and track adoption, behavior change, and culture metrics to measure success.
Leverage data and insights to continuously refine change strategies and improve outcomes.
Capability Building & Enablement
Design and deliver training that supports not just knowledge transfer, but behavioral and mindset shifts.
Coach managers and teams to effectively lead and sustain change.
10+ years of experience leading organizational change, culture transformation, or process adoption initiatives.
Proven ability to drive behavior change and embed new ways of working in complex, cross-functional environments.
Experience partnering with senior leadership to influence culture, alignment, and decision-making.
Strong understanding of change management methodologies (e.g., PROSCI, ACMP), with ability to apply them pragmatically.
Exceptional communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to influence across all levels of the organization.
Experience designing and measuring adoption and culture-related success metrics.
Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (e.g., Communications, Organizational Development, Education).

title: Associate Director, Copay Capabilities
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. The Associate Director, Copay Enablement will play a role within the Copay COE leading the strategic integration and standardization of copay data. This individual will be responsible for copay data strategy, and will partner with cross-functional stakeholders to establish data governance and operations. They will further advance the capabilities and success of the copay COE by translating a foundational data strategy into tools and capabilities that enable the copay team and its cross functional partners to be successful.
Primary responsibilities for this leadership position include, but are not limited to:
Enable the copay center of excellence to be set-up for success within the AbbVie ecosystem, by helping develop robust processes within the COE, and establishing clear ways of working with other AbbVie stakeholders.
Own above-brand stakeholder engagement and communication with key stakeholders.
Foster robust internal relationship with other key stakeholders, including but not limited to Market Access/Trade, Employer Teams, Finance, Patient Services, MABI, etc.
Drive enhanced operational capabilities, improving management and oversight of copay program operations at vendors.
Foster strong data strategy & governance protocols to ensure consistent data operations, stewardship, and reporting.
Plan and execute cross-COE initiatives, establish consistent operational processes & templates, and develop comprehensive knowledge management for all patient access & affordability solutions.
Build a robust KPI tracking and measurement protocol to validate copay program success, and hold external vendors accountable for program operations.

This is a technical role responsible for executing the design, building, testing, and implementation of security systems across our environment, with a specific emphasis on endpoint security and mobility. You will work closely with other members of the Information Security team to identify potential threats and vulnerabilities and develop strategies and solutions to mitigate these risks, securing the end-user device estate and the mobile platforms through which the enterprise increasingly operates, and contributing to our overall information security strategy.
You will join the Business Technology Solutions (BTS) Information Security and Risk Management (ISRM) Architecture organization. Our team translates business objectives and cyber risk strategy into concrete security measures — processes, technologies, and services — across a diverse and complex infrastructure landscape, including on-premises, cloud, and X-as-a-Service models.

Define and evaluate security architecture for the end-user device estate — workstation and laptop hardening, EDR/endpoint protection (e.g., CrowdStrike, Defender), data protection, and configuration baselines.
Advise on mobility security: MDM/UEM (e.g., Microsoft Intune), mobile application management, conditional access, and BYOD posture across iOS and Android.
Perform Security Architecture Reviews — adjudicate submissions, align the risk and controls with the system owner, and ensure review quality.
Deliver Security Architecture Consulting engagements with business partners — own each engagement end to end, with timely turnaround and clear customer communication.
Provide Risk Evidence Review on request, partnering with Risk Management to evaluate control and mitigation effectiveness for risk owners.

Identify and communicate current and emerging security threats and risks; design security architecture elements and propose new or revised measures to mitigate them as they emerge.
Help develop solutions that balance information security needs with the needs of the business, in collaboration with team members and business and IT stakeholders.
Be fluent with AI concepts and incorporate AI into your daily workflows — using AI to accelerate design reviews, threat modeling, documentation, and analysis — targeting improved efficiency, quality, and speed.
Create reusable security-architecture artifacts — reference architectures, design patterns, security guidelines, and security positions — that scale the team's expertise beyond one-off engagements.
Identify recurring problems and build durable systems, patterns, and standards that solve them at the root — not only technical problems, but process and people problems too — so the same issue does not keep resurfacing.
Support training and mentorship of more junior employees as well as employees outside the Information Security Team, as needed.

Bachelor's Degree and 8 years of experience OR Master's Degree and 7 years of experience OR PhD and 3 years of experience.
Demonstrated proficiency with security controls and concepts.
Working knowledge of security frameworks and standards (e.g., NIST, CIS Controls, OWASP, Cloud Security Alliance).
Advanced knowledge of operating systems, networking protocols, systems administration, and security technologies.
Advanced knowledge and application of cybersecurity terminology and concepts, and foundational understanding of the cyber threat landscape and attack vectors.
Understanding of risk management principles and the ability to integrate them into security practices.
Capable of learning new concepts and processes quickly and adapting to a constantly changing environment.
Fluency with AI concepts and demonstrated use of AI tools to improve how you work.
Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving, and analytical skills.
Strong organizational skills with attention to detail.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with a high level of professionalism.
Ability to work independently and effectively as part of a team.
Willingness to be available, as needed, for major and critical security issues.
Demonstrated skills and experience in the following tools: Endpoint protection and detection (EDR/EPP), data protection, and configuration-baseline tooling.
Mobile device and endpoint management (MDM/UEM, e.g., Microsoft Intune), mobile application management, and conditional access.
Operating systems, networking protocols, systems administration, and cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure).
Security control frameworks and the cyber threat landscape and attack vectors.

The Clinical Data Strategy and Operations (CDSO) DMO Lead or Clinical Data Scientist (CDS) serves as the data management domain expert and key strategic partner to the clinical study team. This role owns the data collection strategy, drives implementation, oversees data quality delivery, and supports on-time achievement of key study milestones. As the Data Operations single point of contact for cross-functional stakeholders, the DMO Lead or CDS applies strong project management, risk oversight, and continuous process optimization to enable data quality, inspection readiness, and successful trial delivery.
Responsibilities:
Serves as the CDSO data management subject matter expert and single point of contact for assigned studies, owning data collection, data cleaning, and database lock strategies to enable high-quality, inspection-ready study delivery.
Leads risk-based and continuous data review strategies from study start-up through database lock, leveraging centralized monitoring, statistical review, and clinical data science methodologies to proactively identify and mitigate study risks.
Triages data quality standards across studies to identify trends, drive site-level actions through effective cross-functional communication, and maintain data currency in support of timely, reliable study decisions.
Interprets clinical and operational data, quality metrics, predictive signals, and dashboard outputs to develop data-driven recommendations that strengthen study execution, risk management, patient safety oversight, and quality across the clinical development lifecycle.
Contributes to defining, managing, and monitoring data-driven protocol deviations.

Due Diligence. Act as the primary point of contact for due diligence efforts, and the representative of Commercial BTS within the broader BTS community of M&A practitioners.

About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. At AbbVie, partnership accelerates innovation and helps deliver transformative medicines to patients faster. As Director, Global Alliances, Neuroscience , you will shape and manage strategic external collaborations from discovery through commercialization, with primary responsibility for AbbVie’s Neuroscience partnerships. AbbVie is the industry leader in neuroscience by sales, with a broad and growing portfolio spanning neurodegeneration, psychiatry, neuroinflammation, migraine, and other strategic priorities.
You will lead complex, high-value alliances that advance AbbVie’s neuroscience pipeline and marketed portfolio. As the bridge between AbbVie and its partners, you will foster transparency, strategic alignment, and a shared vision for success across therapeutic areas including neurodegeneration, psychiatry, neuroinflammation, migraine, movement disorders, and other AbbVie neuroscience priorities. You will anticipate challenges, resolve issues, and create the conditions for collaboration that drive scientific and business impact.
You will lead strategic business reviews at key contractual decision points and deliver clear, data-driven recommendations to senior leadership. When needed, you will help negotiate amendments or restructure existing alliances to improve performance and long-term value. You will also support due diligence and business development by assessing, structuring, and negotiating partnership opportunities that strengthen AbbVie’s global pipeline and enterprise strategy.
This role is ideal for a strategic, proactive, and forward-looking relationship builder who thrives at the intersection of science, business, and collaboration and is motivated to make a meaningful impact on patients worldwide.
Major Responsibilities:
Lead Neuroscience Alliances: Advance AbbVie’s neuroscience strategy by aligning AbbVie and its partners around a shared vision, effective governance, and seamless execution across discovery, development, and commercialization. Support alliances across neurodegeneration, psychiatry, neuroinflammation, migraine, movement disorders, and other AbbVie neuroscience priorities. Build trusted relationships and foster joint problem-solving.
Lead Strategic Reviews and Governance: Manage governance forums, including Joint Steering Committees, guide data-informed decisions, assess alliance performance, and recommend actions at key contractual inflection points. Advocate for AbbVie’s alliances, resolve conflicts, and strengthen partner relationships through cross-functional collaboration.
Serve as a Strategic Advisor: Provide forward-looking insights on alliance health, opportunities, and risks to help leadership make data-driven, value-maximizing portfolio decisions.
Support Business Development and Due Diligence: Collaborate with Search and Evaluation and Business Development to evaluate, structure, and negotiate new collaborations. Support due diligence and alliance launch planning to ensure strategic fit, governance readiness, and effective transition to Global Alliances. Represent AbbVie at corporate partnering events to strengthen relationships with current and prospective partners.
Optimize Partnerships: Implement and refine processes, tools, and communication frameworks that improve transparency, consistency, and operational excellence.
Promote Excellence and a Partnering Culture: Establish best-in-class alliance practices and represent AbbVie as a partner of choice in the global biopharma community.

Requires a strong understanding of drug research, development, and commercialization; experience with scientific, regulatory, development, and commercial concepts across early- and late-stage programs; and familiarity with legal agreements and contractual governance.

The Head of AI Solutions leads Quantitative Medicine and Genomics (QM&G)'s AI Solutions organization, the scaling engine that transforms scientific methods, models, and insights into reusable AI-enabled workflows and decision-support capabilities, and is accountable for its strategy, capability roadmap, solution portfolio, operating model, talent, resource allocation, and impact .
The role is also accountable for identifying high-value scientific opportunities, designing reusable solutions around them, and ensuring those solutions move beyond one-off analyses or pilots into capabilities that can be repeatedly applied across QM&G. The Head of AI Solutions brings together scientific problem framing, agentic AI, workflow integration, genomic solutions, and validation to improve the quality, speed, consistency, and scale of scientific decision-making for QM&G’s standardized deliverables.
Reporting into the Head of AI, Bioinformatics and Computational Sciences, this role partners closely with other teams such as Bioinformatics, AI Sciences, Clinical & Real-World Evidence on scientific intelligence creation and with Data & Technology teams to collaboratively scale solutions into products. AI Solutions focuses on the scientific intelligence and workflow layer , partnering with Data organizations on the underlying data, platforms, enterprise engineering and product building.
Key Responsibilities:
Lead and develop QM&G’s AI Solutions capability to transform scientific methods and insights into reusable AI workflows, agents, and decision-support capabilities that accelerate research and portfolio decisions aligned with QM&G’s standardized deliverables.
Define and execute the AI Solutions strategy & portfolio, setting priorities and allocating resources to the highest-impact opportunities aligned with QM&G priorities and the broader AI, Bioinformatics & Computational Sciences strategy.
Define the AI Solutions capability roadmap, translating QM&G’s focus areas into phased milestones, resourcing (build/buy/partner), and timelines from pilot to scaled solution, with KPIs tied to pipeline decision speed and quality.
Establish the organizational model, leadership capacity, and cross-functional delivery mechanisms required to execute a portfolio of high-impact AI solutions aligned with key scientific and business decisions.
Partner with Bioinformatics team to operationalize biological and translational insights, converting validated analyses (e.g., multi-omic target and indication evidence) into reusable, documented pipelines embedded in QM&G’s standardized deliverables.
Collaborate with AI Sciences team to scale novel methods and models, moving from research prototypes to validated, production-ready solutions through shared intake, readiness criteria, and clear handoffs.

description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. This position is part of AbbVie's Information Security & Risk Management (ISRM) team within Business Technology Solutions. The Identity & Access Management (IAM) team is responsible for the development, implementation, and oversight of the organization's IAM strategy, ensuring secure, efficient, and compliant access to systems and data. The NHI and Cloud IAM function addresses one of the fastest-growing attack surfaces in enterprise security—machine identities now outnumber human ones, and the rapid expansion of AI agents is accelerating that trend. This role does not own the AI agent or cloud platforms themselves—those are owned by partner teams across BTS—but it is the IAM team's authoritative voice on how those platforms must integrate with identity governance, and it is accountable for ensuring that no non-human identity operates outside of AbbVie's visibility or control.
Take the next step in your career with an organization that strategically invests in the long-term health of the company, its technology and its people. The AbbVie Business Technology Solutions (BTS) team shapes the digital transformation necessary for our treatments to positively impact patients' lives. In the role of Non-Human Identity and Cloud IAM – Platform Lead, you'll tackle one of the most complex and rapidly evolving challenges in enterprise security: establishing a unified strategy for non-human identities, AI agent governance, and cloud IAM—bridging today's fragmented landscape into a coherent, observable, and future-ready program. This is a senior, highly technical role that requires both architectural depth and the organizational influence to drive accountability across the teams that own AI, agentic, and cloud platforms—ensuring that every non-human identity is visible, governed, and secured from AbbVie's IAM systems.
In this role, you'll be responsible for:
Define and drive the enterprise Non-Human Identity (NHI) strategy—rapidly assessing all in-flight initiatives across the organization, rationalizing overlapping efforts, and establishing a centralized, authoritative governance program covering all machine identities across on-premises, cloud, and agentic environments
Build and maintain a comprehensive NHI registry encompassing service accounts, APIs, bots, application identities, robotic process automation (RPA), and AI agents—ensuring every non-human identity is discovered, inventoried, classified, and continuously governed within IAM systems
Own AbbVie's identity governance posture for AI agents: while the creation and operation of AI agent platforms is owned by other teams, this role is accountable for ensuring those platforms integrate with IAM—so that every AI agent is inventoried in the NHI registry, mapped to its owning human or system identity, governed through appropriate access controls, and visible for security monitoring
Proactively discover and identify new AI agents and agentic workloads as they are introduced across the enterprise; partner with AI platform, cloud, and business teams to ensure timely onboarding into the NHI governance framework, and drive remediations or mappings where gaps exist
Serve as the IAM point of accountability for all agent-related identity questions: defining standards for how agents authenticate, what credentials they use, how those credentials are secured, and how agent activity is observable from an identity and access perspective
Establish centralized NHI observability by driving integration between IAM platforms and external systems—including AWS, Azure, GCP, and agentic platforms (e.g., Microsoft Copilot ecosystem, AWS Bedrock, or similar)—so that IAM maintains a living, authoritative view of all non-human identities regardless of where they originate
Design and implement modern NHI credential security controls including just-in-time (JIT) access, dynamic secrets, short-lived certificates, automated credential rotation, and runtime authentication—reducing standing privilege for machine identities to near zero where possible
Assess the current tooling landscape for NHI and cloud IAM; determine whether existing platforms can be extended or reconfigured, or whether new capabilities are needed; and build a pragmatic, phased modernization roadmap
Own and evolve the Cloud IAM and IGA strategy, closing the integration gap between cloud-native identity platforms (AWS IAM, Azure Entra ID, GCP IAM) and AbbVie's central IAM/IGA tools—ensuring cloud identities, entitlements, and access certifications are governed consistently and automatically
Design cloud identity governance frameworks including role-based access models, entitlement management, access certifications, and least-privilege enforcement across cloud environments
Drive cross-functional alignment across IAM, AI Platform, Cloud, Security Architecture, Compliance, Audit, and business teams—translating complex, fast-moving requirements into executable roadmap priorities and holding partner teams accountable for IAM integration commitments
Establish KPIs and maturity metrics for the NHI and Cloud IAM program, providing executive-level visibility into inventory completeness, risk posture, program progress, and open gaps
Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements (SOX, GDPR, PCI-DSS) for machine identities and cloud access controls; respond to and remediate audit findings

AbbVie Analytical Research & Development (Analytical R&D) is a global analytical scientific organization responsible for all CMC analytical activities related to the development of AbbVie's pharmaceutical products.  Our scope includes AbbVie's diverse pipeline of innovative small molecule medicines and spans from the selection of Discovery candidate molecules to Late Stage Clinical.  We are building a world-class team of scientists and leaders who will drive the advancement of industry-leading analytical capabilities and make meaningful contributions to advance AbbVie's pipeline of innovative medicines.  Careers in AbbVie Analytical R&D provide unique opportunities to work with global and cross-functional teams to drive exceptional science and innovative product development strategies.  We are looking for diverse candidates with strong scientific experience to join the AbbVie Analytical R&D team and can offer exciting and rewarding career opportunities for these candidates.
Position Description:
This Senior Scientist – Solid State Characterization position will be in a technical specialty group - Physical Analytical Chemistry (PAC) withing Analytical R&D.  The PAC group is a global team of experienced and innovative scientists which utilize a diverse set of physical analytical tools to advance CMC development programs by providing insights and driving the understanding of materials, processes, and products.  Additionally, the group contributes to development and justification of control strategies and authors relevant sections of regulatory submissions across all development phases.
We are looking for a subject matter expert in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of drug substances (DS) and drug products (DP), from early form discovery through regulatory filing. The role focuses on single crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), electron diffraction (3D ED/MicroED), Rietveld refinement, quantitative phase analysis (QPA), and phase-appropriate polymorph quantitation methods both in drug substance and drug products. The scientist will work closely with Molecular Profiling Drug Development, Process Chemistry, Formulation, Process Engineering, Analytical, Operations, Quality Assurance and CMC-Regulatory.
Key Responsibilities:
Support new product development with advanced methods development and validations, technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements.

Serve as the PXRD expert for supporting solid form screening, identification, crystallinity, and stability studies; perform indexing, Pawley/Le Bail fitting, Rietveld refinement, and structure determination from powder data.
Perform quantitative phase analysis: Quantify polymorphic and amorphous content in DS and DP using Rietveld, whole-pattern, and multivariate approaches, addressing low drug load, excipient interference, preferred orientation, and micro absorption.
Apply advanced diffraction such as VT/VH-XRPD, in situ, synchrotron, and PDF analysis to study phase transformations and poorly crystalline/amorphous materials.
Apply SCXRD and 3D ED/MicroED structure determination, including absolute configuration and crystal packing of APIs, salts, cocrystals, hydrates, and solvates; generate calculated powder patterns and CIF reports.

Extensive hands-on PXRD experience, including indexing, Rietveld refinement, QPA, and polymorph and amorphous quantitation.

title: Senior AI Development Lead
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join
We're the AI & ML Enablement team in Supply Tech. Teams across Airbnb come to us when they want AI to take over a process, or to ship an AI feature they can trust. We're helping business and field teams use AI to take on high volume-low value tasks, and helping product teams understand whether an AI feature works before it reaches our users. Day to day, we move manual review processes to AI and put people where their judgment matters most. We design new workflows so AI does the work from the start. We also build the labeled datasets that show whether the AI is right, and we keep everything running as models and policies change. Our methods and projects change as the models do, and we expect the scope of this role to grow with them.
The Difference You Will Make
You'd work with whichever team has a problem AI could take on, whether that's a business team with a process that's slow, expensive or inconsistent, or a product team getting an AI feature ready to launch. The job looks much the same either way. You start with how the work really gets done, build an AI version of it, and test it until you trust the results. Then you graduate it and use what worked on the next problem. The mix of projects will keep changing as AI takes on more of the work, so we care more about how you work than about a fixed list of projects. This is a hands-on role. You design and build the workflow, prove it works with data, and ship it with engineering and product.
A Typical Day
Drive the AI workflows and features we support from design to launch, defining the quality bar and measurement plan with engineering, product and business partners.
Prioritize projects by business impact, making trade-offs in partnership with your manager and the business and product leads you support.
Sit with the team that owns a problem, map how the work gets done today, and work out how AI can do it and where people step in for the hard cases.
Design and build AI workflows: write the prompts when needed, set up the pipeline and tooling, and monitor quality and drift once it's live.
Design the evaluation framework: build test sets, define accuracy and agreement metrics, and calibrate LLM judges against human reviewers.
Work with engineers on architecture and tooling decisions, and pressure-test estimates and scope.
Turn unclear guidelines into criteria a reviewer can apply consistently, working with product, Legal and Policy.
Work with subject matter experts to write labeling guidelines and produce human-verified labels on real data.
Run labeling at scale with vendor labeling teams, and check their work against agreement metrics and your own spot checks.
Work with product teams early to agree on what "good enough to launch" means for an AI feature, and bring the evidence and a recommendation for the go/no-go decision.
Build reusable evaluation and workflow components, document what you learn, and get other teams using them so the next team gets to production faster.
Keep our methods current as models, tools and policies change, and recommend what to retire when it stops working.
Your Expertise
8+ years in product or program management, analytics, consulting or applied AI, with a proven record of taking technical programs from idea to production and owning results such as backlog, cycle time or launch speed among others.
You're strong in SQL and in the statistics of quality: accuracy, precision and recall, sampling and reviewer agreement. You pull and analyze the data yourself instead of waiting for a report.
You’ve shipped something built on AI that other people rely on, such as a workflow, an agent or an automation, and you can show the before-and-after numbers. You can tell us where it failed and what you changed.
You're technically fluent enough to pressure-test an engineering estimate, understand how prompts, pipelines and evaluations fit together, and know when a workaround is the right call.
You're curious about how work actually gets done, including the awkward exceptions, and you've taken a messy process and made it measurable. You state the desired result first and measure success in business outcomes, not features shipped.
You have good judgment on quality. You can take messy qualitative feedback, such as reviewer comments or disagreements, and boil it down to what matters and what is worth changing.
You write clearly and can work with sales, operations, PMs and engineers in the same week, getting results through people you don't manage.
You're fine being the first person on a problem, and you try things yourself instead of waiting for someone to build them.
Nice to have
Hands-on Python and API experience, such as scripting data pulls, calling model APIs or building small automations.
Experience with LLM evaluation: building test sets, calibrating LLM judges or fine-tuning models.
Experience with experimentation and measurement, such as A/B tests, metric design and dashboards.
Trust and safety, content moderation, customer support automation, annotation operations or other human-in-the-loop work at scale.
Background in a two-sided marketplace, travel, or another operations-heavy business.

title: Principal Product Manager, Developer Experience and Integration Platform, Amazon Freight
description:
Every shipper and platform that connects to ASCS Shipping and Freight starts the same way: an engineer reads our documentation, requests credentials, and tries to make a first successful call or EDI transmission. When that path takes weeks instead of days, shippers delay launch and revenue waits. We are hiring a Principal Product Manager - Technical to make ASCS Shipping and Freight the simplest logistics provider in the industry to integrate with, across both API and EDI.
You will own the strategy and roadmap for how developers onboard and integrate with ASCS Shipping and Freight. The role spans two integration models. 1P integrations are custom, direct integrations with large shippers, where their engineering teams connect enterprise systems to our APIs or EDI. 3P integrations are platform partnerships with ecommerce platforms, fulfillment providers, multi-carrier platforms, and TMS and WMS providers, where one integration unlocks shipping for thousands of merchants. You will define a path that serves both: repeatable and self-service for platforms, and configurable without becoming bespoke engineering for large shippers.
Your charter covers four areas. First, simplify and streamline developer onboarding, from developer registration, data-access approval, and credential management through sandbox testing, certification, and go-live. Second, own the developer documentation portal as a product, including API reference, EDI implementation guides, code samples, Postman collections, and changelogs. Third, use AI to cut time to onboard and integrate, including AI assistants that answer developer questions, generate integration code and EDI mappings, diagnose failed calls, and docs that AI coding tools can consume directly. Fourth, own the integration product strategy across API and EDI, closing capability gaps between the two channels.
You will work as a peer to the Solutions Architect (SA) team, who lead hands-on technical engagements with shippers and partners, and with Support Engineering, whose support-contact data shows where developers get stuck. SAs and Support Engineering bring direct insight into where integrations stall, and you turn those patterns into product, documentation, and tooling that remove the need for the next escalation. The goal is that SAs spend their time on the most complex, highest-value launches while standard integrations complete through self-service.
This is a deeply technical role. You will review API designs, EDI transaction mappings, and authentication models with principal engineers and Solutions Architects as a peer, and you will build working calls yourself to test the experience a developer gets. You will also influence leaders across the org whose teams build the capabilities developers integrate with.
We measure success by developer outcomes: time from registration to first successful call, time from kickoff to production go-live for 1P and 3P integrations, percentage of standard integrations completed through self-service, integration completion rate, sandbox-to-production parity, API and EDI error rates, and integration-related support contacts. You will set the baselines and targets, and report progress in weekly and monthly business reviews.
Key job responsibilities
Define the strategy for developer experience and integrations across API and EDI for ASCS Shipping and Amazon Freight, and secure alignment from engineering, Solutions Architecture, business development, partnerships, and senior leadership.
Map and instrument every step of the integration journey for 1P and 3P developers and remove the largest sources of friction first: developer registration, data-access approval, and credential lifecycle, including identity verification requests, audit pauses, and credential expiry.

Define and launch AI capabilities that cut time to integrate, such as a developer assistant trained on our docs, automated EDI mapping and validation, AI-generated sample code, failed-call diagnosis, and machine-readable docs and MCP servers for AI coding tools.
Define the EDI roadmap (for example, ANSI X12 tender, status, and invoice transactions) and close capability gaps between EDI and API across business lines.
Own the percentage of standard integrations completed through self-service. Run a shared blocker list with the Solutions Architect and Support Engineering teams, prioritize fixes, and convert custom enterprise requirements into configurable, reusable capabilities, so the next large shipper launches faster than the last.
Partner with Business Development and Solutions Architects to prioritize 3P platform integrations by shipper reach. Own the technical content of partner certification, including what gets tested, the validation tooling, and the pass criteria, in support of the certification program run by Partnerships.
Own outbound communication of built and planned enhancements to 1P shippers and 3P partners, including roadmap previews, release communications, enablement, and adoption tracking. Share field-level guidance with partners only after the owning team confirms deployment.
Partner with the product leaders who own account modeling, account lifecycle, centralized KYC, and segmentation, so developer onboarding and credential approval run on the same account and identity foundations across business lines.
Own the integration funnel metrics, run voice-of-developer programs, analyze support contacts, and use the results to set priorities.
Write PRFAQs, PRDs, and launch plans, coordinate developer communications and deprecations, and mentor product managers on technical product practice.

description:
When a shipper moves a truckload with Amazon Freight, they expect the load to be scheduled, tracked, and delivered without having to chase anyone. Today, too much of that experience depends on manual work. Support associates switch between many tools to find information, repetitive tasks stay manual, and some work happens outside our systems where no one can see it, measure it, or automate it. Shippers feel the result as slow answers and repeat contacts. We are hiring a Principal Product Manager - Technical to change that: to make shipper support for Amazon Freight fast, measurable, and increasingly automated.
You will own the multi-year product strategy and roadmap for the Amazon Freight shipper support experience, covering the platform, automation, and AI that associates use to resolve shipper issues. Your mandate has three parts. First, eliminate the reasons shippers contact us, by finding root causes in scheduling, tendering, tracking, disruptions, and billing and driving fixes upstream with the teams that own them. Second, make every piece of operational work visible and owned, by consolidating work done in other systems into a single operator console and ensuring every task has an owner, a queue, and a service level. Third, automate the work that does not need human judgment, using rule-based automation first and AI agents where they add value.
The heart of this role is a continuous automation flywheel. You will define the architecture for a framework that captures task-level data across operational workflows (what work is done, why, and how long it takes), then run a repeatable cycle of discover, document, model, measure, build, and automate. You will use that data and AI to find and rank automation candidates, launch rule-based automation for deterministic tasks in areas like scheduling, disruption recovery, trailer pool management, and proactive shipper communications, and route exceptions to the right operator. Every eliminated task is recorded, so the team can prove impact and reinvest the time saved.
This is a technical role. You will work with engineers on the operator platform architecture, the data model for task capture, integrations with the operational systems that work moves out of, and the design of AI agents that retrieve information, draft responses, and take actions safely. You will make build-versus-reuse decisions, weigh trade-offs between rule-based and AI approaches, and set the guardrails for automation.
You will partner closely with Amazon Freight support operations leaders, who own priorities and targets for their teams, and with engineering, operations, policy, and the product teams that own scheduling, execution, and disruption management. You propose solutions backed by data; operations validates them; engineering builds them. You will work as a peer to the Amazon Shipping support product leader, sharing platforms, patterns, and AI capabilities so that what works in one business scales to the other.
We measure success with the same metrics as our other shipper support products: support contacts per load, first-contact resolution, shipper satisfaction (CSAT), automation rate, average handle time, and annual cost savings. Because measurable work comes first, you will also own input metrics that show the work is visible: share of associate work captured in the operator console, share of contacts with a recorded reason, tasks with an owner and service level, and tasks eliminated through automation. title: Senior Product Manager, Account Lifecycle, Segmentation, and KYC, ASCS Shipping and Freight
description:
Every shipper relationship with ASCS Shipping and Freight runs on its account: who the shipper is, what legal entity stands behind them, which segment they belong to, and where they are in their lifecycle. We are hiring a Senior Product Manager to build that foundation once, for Amazon Shipping and Amazon Freight.
You will own three product areas. First, centralized Know Your Customer (KYC): a single verification of a shipper's business identity and legal entity that every ASCS Shipping and Freight business line trusts and reuses, so a shipper verified once never repeats the process. Second, account lifecycle management: the states, transitions, and controls that govern an account from registration through activation, growth, dormancy, reactivation, suspension, and closure. Third, segmentation: a consistent, data-driven definition of shipper segments that sales, onboarding, pricing, support, and operations use to tailor the experience each shipper receives.

You will own the roadmap and delivery for your three areas, write the PRFAQs and PRDs, and partner with engineering, compliance, risk, sales operations, and product teams to launch them. Your work starts with the crawl phase: standing up centralized KYC and the legal-entity foundation, and cleaning existing account data so it meets the new standard.
We measure success by shipper and business outcomes: time to complete verification, share of shippers verified once and reused across business lines, duplicate account rate, accounts in a valid lifecycle state, segment coverage and accuracy, and contacts and manual work caused by account data issues. You will set the baselines and targets, and report progress in weekly and monthly business reviews.

Deliver centralized KYC by defining requirements for a single business identity and legal-entity verification that Amazon Shipping and Amazon Freight reuse. title: Senior Product Manager, Shipper Communications, ASCS Shipping and Freight
description:
Shippers want to hear from us when something matters to their business: a missed pickup, a delayed load, an exception they need to act on, or a new capability that helps them ship. Today, they hear from us through many separate teams and systems. Messages overlap, arrive on channels the shipper does not watch, or arrive after the shipper has already called support to find out what happened. We are hiring a Senior Product Manager to give shippers one coordinated voice from ASCS Shipping and Freight, across Amazon Shipping and Amazon Freight.
You will own the product strategy and roadmap for shipper communications, covering both what reaches shippers and what reaches the internal operators and account managers who act on their behalf. Your charter has three parts. First, build the communications platform: the shared capability that every team uses to send notifications to shippers and to internal teams, with templates, routing, delivery across channels such as email, SMS, in-app, mobile push, and partner feeds. Second, source the signals: partner with operations, execution, account, billing, and marketing teams to identify the events that shippers need to know about, define a taxonomy for each event (severity, audience, channel, and how fast it must arrive), and route each signal to the right audience: the shipper, the operator who resolves the issue, the account manager who owns the relationship, or all three. Third, protect the shipper's attention: set the rules that consolidate, prioritize, and suppress messages so shippers are not overloaded with siloed communications, and deliver every message on the shipper's preferred channel.
You will be the owner of the shipper communications experience, not the author of every message. Marketing owns campaign content and brand standards, and operational teams own the quality of the signals they detect. You will own the platform, the event taxonomy, the preference and frequency rules, and the outcome metrics, and you will set the governance that every sending team follows.
We measure success by shipper outcomes: the share of shipper-impacting disruptions where we notify the shipper before they contact support, notification delivery within the target time for each severity and audience, the share of issues where the responsible operator or account manager is alerted before the shipper escalates, the share of shippers with communication preferences set, engagement and action rates, opt-out rates, communication volume per shipper, and support contacts avoided through proactive communication. You will set the baselines and targets, and report progress in weekly and monthly business reviews.

Partner with operations, execution, account management, billing, and marketing teams to identify the events shippers need to know about, and define a taxonomy for each event that sets severity, audience, channel, and target delivery time.
Define and deliver a shipper preference center so each shipper chooses which communications they receive, on which channel, and for which users and locations in their account.
Set frequency, consolidation, and suppression rules so related messages combine into one, lower-priority messages wait, and no shipper receives duplicate or conflicting communications from different teams.
Establish governance for every team that sends shipper communications, including template standards, an inventory of active templates, review of new communication requests, and retirement of outdated or overlapping messages.
Own the notifications that reach internal operators and account managers, so the right person is alerted when an issue needs action or a personal follow-up, and can see everything each shipper has been told.

description:
AWS operates the world's largest fleet of GPU-accelerated servers powering AI/ML workloads at cloud scale. Our team designs, builds, and operates this fleet — solving systemic hardware issues and building systems that detect and prevent recurrence so customers experience the highest quality of service.
We are seeking a Senior Technical Program Manager (hardware) to drive end-to-end delivery of GPU-accelerated servers across our global fleet. You will own programs where the critical path runs through silicon, firmware, and software teams simultaneously. You will translate ambiguity into structure: turning a fleet telemetry signal into a corrective action plan with quantified failure rates, a customer requirement into a new platform milestone with EVT/DVT/PVT gates, or a manufacturing escape into a design change with updated validation criteria. You will drive decisions on program trade-offs — adjusting scope when qualification gates slip, balancing deployment speed against fleet risk, and determining when to accept interim mitigations instead of holding for root-cause fixes. When a large scale of GPU servers depend on your program landing on time, you are the one ensuring hardware readiness, qualification completeness, and operational handoff happen without gaps.
Why You Will Love It
The world's most advanced frontier models are trained on the platforms you help build. Your programs launch the GPU servers that power the largest AI/ML workloads on the planet. You will see your decisions reflected in fleet reliability metrics within weeks of deployment. The team is small and high-trust — you own programs end to end from concept through production, with direct access to leadership and engineering alike.
The Ideal Candidate
You have deep technical intuition across hardware and software — enough to challenge engineering decisions, not just track them. You thrive in ambiguity, bringing structure to programs where requirements, timelines, and dependencies are still forming. You align priorities across teams in different organizations, and you escalate with data, not noise. You actively mentor and develop others — TPMs and engineers alike. You contribute to hiring, promotion assessments, and raising the bar for program management practices in your organization.
Key job responsibilities
Strategy & Mechanisms
* Define program strategy, objectives, and success criteria; influence resource allocation and priority decisions across engineering workstreams to align with organizational goals
* Build and own mechanisms for program visibility — defining metrics, dashboards, and review cadences that enable data-driven decisions and early risk detection
* Streamline delivery processes across teams; identify and eliminate dependencies, redundant gates, or coordination overhead that slow velocity
Requirements & Planning
* Facilitate requirements gathering with internal customers; develop Technical Requirements Documents (TRDs) covering server specs, rack configurations, PCIe topology, power/cooling topology, and SKU definitions

Execution & Coordination
* Drive cross-functional alignment across hardware, firmware (BIOS, BMC, CPLD), software, and operations teams through design reviews, manufacturing readiness and production readiness for fleet deployment.

* Identify blockers early, escalate dependencies before they impact critical path, and facilitate technical trade-off decisions across engineering workstreams.

* Challenge technical workstreams to surface risks early; quantify impact to schedule and reliability (annualized failure rate targets, availability SLAs) with proposed mitigations

* Conduct knowledge transfer and document lessons learned; ensure operational readiness including automation, monitoring, and runbook completeness for production handoff

You should be comfortable operating in ambiguity, defining quality bars where none exist yet, and delivering rigorous results on tight schedules.

title: Engineering Manager, Private Cloud Compute Inference Routing
description:
At Apple, iCloud Platform Engineering builds the server stack behind Push Notifications, iMessage, FaceTime, iCloud, iCloud Private Relay and Private Cloud Compute (PCC), the backbone of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence. We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead PCC inference routing. These systems send every inference request to the right compute across a global, multi-region fleet, while keeping latency low, availability high and PCC's privacy guarantees intact.
This is a technically grounded leadership role for someone who thrives at scale, can bring clarity to complex and fast-changing environments, and is energized by building both systems and teams. You'll guide architectural direction, scale operational practices and develop the engineers and leaders who will shape how Apple delivers cloud inference.
Routing LLM inference at Apple's scale takes systems that adapt to changing demand, available capacity and failures while keeping latency low and accelerator utilization high. As the fleet grows across regions and cells, routing must account for capacity and health across the whole fleet, not just a single site. PCC adds a basic architectural requirement: request content stays encrypted outside trusted compute nodes. You'll lead the design of routing and scheduling strategies within this privacy model. Together with inference and security teams, you'll evaluate techniques such as cache-aware request placement and prefill/decode disaggregation. Your scope includes the inference AI gateway layer, where requests are authenticated, metered, prioritized and streamed back to clients, all without exposing request content.
This work has broad reach. Every improvement to routing makes Siri AI and Apple Intelligence faster and more reliable, and makes better use of Apple's inference capacity. In your first year, you'll be expected to grow a high-performing organization, set a clear technical roadmap, and measurably improve routing latency, availability and fleet utilization.

title: Member Experience Operations, Training & Quality
description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As part of our Member Experience team, you will own quality assurance and training for our frontline support team. You'll make sure every member who reaches out to Base gets accurate, clear, and empathetic help, no matter who picks up. This role blends program ownership with hands-on coaching. You'll build the scorecards, curriculum, and feedback loops that help new agents ramp quickly and help tenured agents keep getting better. You will use data, member feedback, and direct observation to find what's working and fix what isn't, so quality holds up as our member base grows.

 

What You’ll Do

 - Quality assurance scorecard – Build and maintain rubrics across phone, email, chat, and text that measure accuracy, empathy, and resolution.

 - Interaction reviews – Build and maintain a structured program for you and team leads to review a consistent sample of member interactions for every agent every week, leveraging AI to build systems as needed.

 - Calibration – Run regular calibration sessions with team leads and others, so every reviewer grades to the same standard. Manage the process for agents to ask questions about or dispute their scores.

 - Coaching and feedback – Turn QA results into agent-shareable scores and specific, actionable coaching feedback. Partner with team leads on 1:1s and performance improvement plans, and give agents clear, kind feedback they can act on.

 - New hire onboarding – Design and run training for new agents, from classroom learning to shadowing to nesting to self-sufficiency. Set clear ramp milestones and certify agents before they work independently.

 - Ongoing training – Build continuing education for the whole team: refreshers, product and policy updates, and advanced skills like de-escalation and handling hard conversations. Track completion and measure whether training changes results.

 - Knowledge management – Keep the knowledge base, standard operating procedures (SOPs), call guides, and saved reply templates accurate and current. Make sure agents always know where to find the right answer.

 - Metrics and reporting – Track and report on QA scores, member satisfaction (CSAT), first contact resolution (FCR), and new hire ramp time. Connect QA findings to member outcomes and share trends with leadership.

 - Root cause analysis – Find patterns in QA results and member feedback. Separate training gaps from process, tooling, and product issues, and drive the fix at the source.

 - Compliance and risk – Make sure agents follow policies on contracts, billing, and disclosures. Flag risks early and escalate them to Legal and Finance.

 - Voice of the member – Share what you see in member interactions to help shape better experiences, services, and policies across the company.

 - Launch readiness – Partner with other teams so agents are trained and ready before new policies, features, and launches reach members.

 

What You'll Bring

 - 2-8+ years of experience in quality assurance, training, or enablement for a customer support, contact center, or customer success team.

 - Hands-on experience building QA scorecards, running calibration sessions, and turning review results into coaching plans.

 - Experience designing and delivering training, including new hire onboarding and ongoing skill development.

 - Coaching skills that change behavior: direct, kind, and specific feedback that agents trust.

 - Comfort with data. You can analyze QA scores, CSAT, FCR, and NPS, then turn what you find into clear recommendations.

 - Comfort owning outcomes end-to-end, as motivated to fix the root cause as to improve the individual interaction.

 - Strong writing skills with excellent grammar, tone, and clarity for training materials, SOPs, and feedback.

 - Confidence facilitating, from 1:1 coaching sessions to full-team trainings.

 - Tech savvy, with experience in help desk platforms, QA tools, learning management systems, and knowledge bases, and a knack for quickly mastering new ones.

 - Not afraid to get on the front line. You'll listen to calls, read tickets, and take contacts yourself to understand what agents face.

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and a fast-paced environment to quickly adapt to changes.

 - Team player motivated by the mission who always puts the company's best interests first.

 

About the Team

The Member Experience team is the face of Base to our members—and the voice of our members back to Base. We’re deeply customer-obsessed and uniquely cross-functional, with a strong understanding of what every team does and how it all connects. By seeing firsthand what’s working well and what should be improved, we surface insights that help inform what the business builds and prioritizes next. Every day brings a new challenge, balancing high ownership and accountability with constant collaboration and support from the team.

title: Lead Deployment Partner
description:
About CADDi
CADDi is the Manufacturing AI Data Platform transforming a trillion-dollar global industry. By unifying fragmented engineering, procurement, production, and quality data, we empower enterprise manufacturers and their AI agents to make faster, smarter decisions every day.
Founded in 2017 with dual headquarters in Chicago and Tokyo, CADDi serves manufacturing leaders across more than 20 countries. We recently announced a $114M Series D funding round at a $1.2B valuation, bringing total funding to $234M, backed by top-tier investors including Salesforce Ventures, Woven Capital, and Atomico.
We are expanding our North American operations rapidly and building next-generation products like CADDi Explorer and CADDi Agent. If you are eager to solve hard data and engineering problems while scaling a fast-growing unicorn, we’d love to talk.
The role
As a Deployment Partner, you own a customer from first discovery through a live, adopted workflow, and then through expansion across the enterprise. You work directly with the people who run the plant floor, procurement, quality, and engineering from operational management up to the C-suite deciding where AI fits in their business.
You work with the CADDi AI Data Platform and suite of workflow-specific products a configurable tool you capitalize on for each customer. You are accountable for their success end-to-end: time-to-value, the deployment of the solutions we promised, the measurable value they see enterprise-wide, and the renewal that follows.
The role folds pre-sales, customer success, and data expertise into a single owner, working alongside an Account Executive on the commercial side and Forward Deployed Engineers who build the technical pieces beyond what you configure.
What you’ll do
Understand the customer
Deployment Partners take the deepest, most strategic accounts, leading value validation, designing the technical solution, orchestrating Forward Deployed Engineers, and driving change at the executive level.
Meet with cross-functional teams across engineering, procurement, quality, and operations onsite as needed to learn how they work and where time and money are lost.
Advise customer leaders, from operational management to the C-suite, on where AI and a shared data foundation create the most value, and agree on what success means for their business.
Identify the data that matters (drawings, quotes, part records, supplier data) and model it into the platform, working with Forward Deployed Engineers where deeper integration is needed.
Partner with Sales before the deal closes to validate value with real customer data and show an early, concrete win. Build and deliver tailored demos for prospects and existing customers.
Deploy and drive adoption
Own the deployment plan from scoping to production, coordinating customer stakeholders across business units, IT, procurement, and compliance.
Define the semantic layer for the customer’s data, configure the data layer, and build the Explorer configuration and plugins the deployment needs, reusing existing configurations, plugins, and libraries wherever possible to move fast.
Deploy CADDi’s workflow products for each user group and shape deployments of CADDi Agent, run training and adoption sessions
Orchestrate Forward Deployed Engineers on the technical gap between the standard platform and what the customer needs, such as data pipelines, custom integrations, and advanced analytics.
Define the success metrics and quality bar for each deployment, track them, and run QBRs to customer and CADDi leadership.
Own operations after go-live and grow the account
Own the operational health of every live deployment, so environments, data pipelines, configurations, and access stay reliable as the customer’s data, users, and processes change
Design and quantify ROI, and present findings to audiences from shop-floor users to the executive team to drive decisions and action.
Identify expansion opportunities within accounts and work with the Account Executive to turn them into new business, including upsell, cross-sell, and global rollout.
Bring what you see in the field back to Product and Engineering so it shapes the roadmap, and return reusable configurations and learnings to the shared library so the next deployment is faster.
What we value
Curiosity and ownership: you keep digging past the first answer, and you follow through on every one of several complex, visible projects at once.
Comfort with ambiguity: you do your best work in messy, unstructured customer environments, and you know when to lead and when to support.
Bias for speed: you would rather put something real in front of users this week than something perfect next quarter.

What we’re looking for
8+ years in a customer-facing technical role (solutions consulting, implementation, forward-deployed engineering, analytics consulting, or similar), with a track record of owning complex deployments end-to-end and driving measurable adoption and expansion.
Strong written and verbal communication with both technical and non-technical audiences, from operational management up to the C-suite.
Comfort structuring messy, multi-source data into clear models defining semantics and relationships is central to this role.
Working knowledge of Python, SQL, or similar tools for exploring data, and comfort reading API documentation and discussing system architecture with engineers, is a nice-to-have.
Manufacturing, industrial, or supply chain experience is a plus.
Willingness to work from our Chicago office and travel [40–60%].
Bilingual Japanese/English is a plus.
US Person status / ITAR eligibility is a plus.
Work environment: In-office five days a week at our Chicago, IL office.

About the Team
The Dasher & Logistics team ensures every delivery is completed with speed, accuracy, and a positive experience for consumers, merchants, and Dashers. We own the health of DoorDash’s delivery network, including supply and demand, cost and quality, Dasher pay and incentives, Dasher acquisition and retention, assignment and batching, and real-time operations.
Within Strategy & Operations, Dasher & Logistics is made up of teams that each own part of this system, such as Network Strategy, US Markets, Regulated Markets, Canada, Supply, Pay & Efficiency, and Live Ops. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, Analytics, Finance, Marketing, and Operations to run and improve one of the largest last-mile logistics networks in the world.
About the Role
We’re hiring a Senior Manager, Strategy & Operations to own a meaningful part of the Dasher & Logistics network end-to-end. Depending on the team, that could be how we invest in Dasher supply, the health of every US market, our most complex regulated markets, or the delivery network for an entire country. You will be accountable for the cost-to-quality tradeoff in your area: faster, more reliable deliveries at the same cost, or the same quality at a lower cost.
You will find where the network underperforms, design and test the fix, and work with Product and Engineering to build it into how the network runs. You will make tradeoff decisions across Dasher earnings, consumer experience, merchant reliability, and unit economics, and bring clear recommendations to senior leadership. Design and run experiments that lead to clear decisions, then scale what works across markets
Partner with Product, Engineering, and Analytics to turn manual wins into durable product and system changes
Make thoughtful tradeoff decisions between cost, growth, and customer experience to protect long-term marketplace health
Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team, and grow the next set of leaders at DoorDash
Help keep the network running smoothly during incidents, severe weather, and holidays alongside our Live Ops partners

The team operates like a startup inside a large company, so the role combines strategy with hands-on execution and you have to be a player coach. The Director will test new channels, formats and partnerships ahead of the category, and will build an agentic marketing team that lets a small group operate at the scale of a much larger one.
POSITION LOCATION:
This position can be based at our global headquarters in Deerfield, Illinois, in San Francisco, California, or remote within the United States.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Strategy, Brand & Team
Set a bold growth strategy, plan and budget for Yale and August, with clear OKRs for revenue, share, activation and brand health, and a clear point of view on where the next wave of customers and revenue will come from.
Define a clear, differentiated brand position and set the creative standard for every campaign, launch and channel, holding internal teams and agencies to it.
Build and grow an agentic marketing team spanning creative, digital, and product and channel marketing for B2C and Pro/B2B, using AI agents for analytics, reporting, content and campaign operations; manage agency partners across media, creative, PR and web.
Brand Growth & Innovation
Build and scale the Yale and August brands in new and innovative ways, going beyond category-standard marketing to earn attention, advocacy and loyalty, and making home security feel personal rather than transactional.
Launch and grow creator, influencer, community and customer-advocacy programs and turn them into a repeatable engine for acquisition and word of mouth.
Build brand partnerships and ecosystem co-marketing with smart home platforms, builders, property managers, insurers and lifestyle brands that open new customer segments and routes to market.
