ITW Construction provides a variety of fastening systems and truss products for commercial, residential, and remodeling/renovation segments. The GTU innovates, develops, and manufactures through our Customer Back Innovation process best-in-class Power Fastening Systems for the global construction market. Our highly differentiated tools are specified to be used in a variety of applications including wood framing, wood trim, and steel to concrete installations. Tools, and related fasteners, account for a significant portion of total segment revenues
The NPD Senior Mechanical Design Engineer plays a key role in driving mechanical design execution across one or more new product development programs, with responsibility for the design and development of cordless and pneumatic power fastening tools primarily used in wood and concrete applications. This position emphasizes deep hands-on technical contribution and problem-solving skills while progressively taking ownership of project-level decision-making, design direction, and coordination across functions. The role supports the delivery of robust, high-quality, and manufacturable mechanical solutions, while developing leadership capability through increasing responsibility for project leadership and mentoring. The ideal candidate brings strong mechanical design expertise, a proactive ownership mindset, demonstrated technical excellence and cross-functional influence.
Core Responsibilities
Leads project-level mechanical design execution, leveraging strong technical judgment and project planning skills to define scope, coordinate task-level resources, and deliver committed program objectives on time and within established constraints.
Owns concept development and detailed design activities, translating customer and market inputs into viable mechanical concepts, developing and refining designs in 3D CAD, and iterating based on internal and external feedback to achieve performance, cost, and schedule goals.
Performs and drives critical design analyses such as DFMEA, Design of Experiments, Tolerance Stack-ups, and serviceability assessments to proactively identify risks and ensure alignment with product requirements and specifications.
Takes responsibility for the integrated mechanical design of electro-mechanical devices and subsystems used in power fastening systems, ensuring proper layout, interface definition, design integration, validation, and documentation.
Coordinates prototype builds and validation activities, overseeing the production of prototypes and test units and supporting transition to manufacturing while ensuring quality standards, delivery schedules, and cost targets are met.
Identifies, recommends, and implements design improvements, tracking corrective actions to resolve failures, enhance reliability, and prevent recurrence of product or system malfunctions.
Supports manufacturing process selection and supplier engagement, contributing to make/buy decisions and process definition to deliver robust, cost-effective products that meet market needs.
Executes complex assignments with increasing autonomy, demonstrating initiative, sound engineering judgment, and ownership while progressively expanding influence and leadership within the project team.
Partners closely with cross-functional teams including marketing, purchasing, manufacturing, quality, and suppliers to define project scope, assess cost targets, and ensure manufacturing feasibility throughout development.
Qualifications
BS in Mechanical / Mechatronics Engineering or related field (master’s Preferred)
8+ years of relevant product mechanical - design, including 2+ years in product development
Demonstrated experience working within structured, stage‑based product development frameworks,
Proficiency in CAD Design/Modeling Tools (preferred Pro/Engineer CREO-11)
Familiarity with PLM systems (Windchill) and version control.
Strong understanding of Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) tools.
Demonstrated design capability, problem solving skills and ability to understand and trouble shoot electro-mechanical equipment.
Demonstrated experience of structured problem‑solving and continuous improvement methodologies, including A3’s Problem Solving, 8D, Fishbone (Ishikawa), cause‑and‑effect diagrams & 5 Why’s.
Experience in Leading design reviews, DFMEA, PFMEA, DVP&R, and root cause analysis sessions.
Strong understanding of modeling and simulation tools capabilities (FEA, CFD)
Advanced understanding of statistical tools such as FRD, DOE, COV, SPC, Pareto Analysis, etc.
Strong understanding of materials, manufacturing processes, and mechanical analysis including, plastic injection, stamping, aluminum, casting, machining, etc.
Experience in cross-functional collaboration to industrialize new products.
Experience with prototyping, testing, and production tooling.
Project management experience is a plus.
Domestic and International travel: 10-15%

Standard office and lab environment.
Occasional travel to suppliers, manufacturing sites, or testing facilities.

title: Assembly Technician 1
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position:
The primary objective for this person is to assemble a variety of products, meeting quality and productivity goals, within a manufacturing work environment. This person would work closely with fellow team members, the area Lead, and the supervisor to achieve team performance goals in the areas of Efficiency, DPU, Hours Reporting Accuracy, Scrap, Inventory Accuracy, and Time Lost Accuracy. Goals are set in each of these areas for each quarter and overall team performance is measured against them.
Roles and Responsibilities :
• Assemble a variety of products according to standard work instructions and prints.
• Operate and set up (as needed), production equipment/fixtures.
• Become proficient at multiple assembly tasks while meeting requirements for workmanship, safety and productivity.
• Perform preparation work such as line clearance and changeover.
• Perform inspection of own and other’s work. Perform simple repairs on own or other’s work.
• Mentor others in areas of expertise (as needed).
• Properly complete manufacturing documentation. Initiate basic material requests, report quality issues, report efficiency, record measurements as needed. May report work order information into computer.
• Maintain the accuracy of identification and count of point-of-use materials. Accurately determine and report material shortages.
• Follow all corporate, regulatory, safety and production policies and procedures.
• Maintain an excellent attendance record.
• Perform other duties as assigned.
Skill/Job Requirements:
• Education: High school diploma or equivalent.
• Experience: 0 – 1 year previous mechanical assembly experience preferred.
• Language Skills: Ability to read, write and understand English. Ability to read and comprehend instructions, short correspondence, and memos. Ability to write simple correspondence. Ability to effectively present information in one-on-one and small group situations to other employees, supervisors, or engineers.
• Mathematical Skills: Ability to add and subtract multi-digit numbers (including decimals); to multiply and divide; to find averages, percentages and ranges. Ability to determine the minimum, maximum and nominal value when provided with a specification and a tolerance. Ability to perform basic math on a calculator.
• Reasoning Ability: Ability to apply commonsense understanding to carry out instructions. Ability to report quality issues. Ability to suggest simple process improvements.
• Computer skills: Ability to use personal computers as part of daily work. Ability to use on-line documentation.
• Other skills and abilities: Ability to work varying shifts. Must have the ability to complete training courses. Ability to work in a team environment. Ability to use clocks, timers, tools, and rulers. Ability to work in a controlled environment room (i.e. clean room), this includes wearing clean room gowns, head caps, booties as well as meeting other clean room standards such as no jewelry or make-up.

title: Creative Operations Lead
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
The Creative Operations Lead is a key role within Brand & Creative responsible for the operational strategy and continuity of the Creative Operations and Events function. The role brings together planning, prioritization, resource alignment, capacity forecasting, governance, reporting, technology, workflow optimization, infrastructure, enablement, and cross-functional coordination. As the central operations partner to Brand & Creative leadership and other cross-functional partners, this position reduces duplication, improves visibility, and directs resources toward the highest-priority business needs. Through proactive planning, clear communication, and transparency, the role enables timely decisions and effective expectation management across Brand & Creative.
Essential Job Duties
Lead Creative Operations planning and governance across Brand & Creative, establishing clear priorities, decision forums, and communication practices that align work with business objectives and leadership priorities, in partnership with Creative Solutions Management and Creative Project Management.
Own capacity and forecasting models that give visibility into project volume, resource demand, workload balance, constraints, and future staffing needs, in partnership with Creative Solutions Management, Creative Project Management, and Brand & Creative functional teams.
Design, document, and continuously improve scalable workflows, intake processes, operating rhythms, templates, and playbooks that drive efficient, consistent ways of working.
Own data integrity, dashboards, and reporting across Workfront, Smartsheet, and related tools, and translate operational data and stakeholder feedback into recommendations that help leadership identify gaps, assess resource implications, and make informed tradeoff decisions.
Lead Creative Operations technology strategy, including systems integration, automation, administration, and adoption of the tools that enable scalable operations.
Develop and implement a global Brand & Creative asset management system, including governance, metadata standards, permissions, lifecycle management, and adoption across regions and functions, in partnership with Global Marketing Operations and Brand & Creative Studio.
Oversee operational delivery by monitoring milestones, dependencies, risks, and cross-functional handoffs; driving timely escalation and resolution; and leading post-project reviews that turn lessons learned into operational improvements.
Own centralized budget, purchase order, and procurement planning, tracking, and coordination; partner with Procurement to establish and maintain an agency overflow roster (scope alignment, utilization, performance, and readiness), supported by Brand & Creative agency onboarding; and work with leadership on operating model improvements and alignment of capabilities to evolving Global Marketing priorities.
Build, implement, and maintain the onboarding strategy and hubs for Brand & Creative, including new team members and agency partners, providing the guidance, processes, tools, and training needed to onboard quickly and work consistently across Brand & Creative.
Develop and maintain resource libraries, process documentation, and training resources, and model operational discipline and inclusive collaboration while mentoring others on tools, processes, governance, and accountability.
Required Skills and Experience
12+ years of experience in creative operations, brand operations, marketing operations, business operations, program management, strategy, or related operational leadership roles.
Proven track record leading strategic operational initiatives from concept through implementation, including process design, workflow optimization, governance, change management, and stakeholder adoption, and building the infrastructure, onboarding resources, and training materials that make new ways of working scalable.
Strong experience with annual and quarterly planning, intake and prioritization, resource alignment, capacity forecasting, and operational reporting.
Experience owning or optimizing operational tools such as Workfront, Smartsheet, dashboards, or similar project, portfolio, and collaboration platforms.
Demonstrated ability to apply AI-enabled tools to improve process efficiency, strengthen analysis, identify insights, and support informed decision-making while maintaining appropriate data quality, governance, and human oversight.
Excellent communication, executive presence, writing, and facilitation skills, with the ability to influence senior leaders, lead through change, simplify complex work, and coach others.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; able to interpret data, identify operational gaps, recommend practical solutions, and support data-informed decisions in a complex and evolving environment.
Experience partnering with creative, marketing, finance, regulatory, regional, and project management teams to align shared goals and foster collaboration, accountability, and trust.
Required Education and Training
BA/BS degree preferred in Business, Marketing, Communications, Operations, or a related field; equivalent experience may be considered.
Working Conditions
Standard office environment. Role requires frequent cross-functional collaboration, extended computer use, and occasional travel for business planning, team meetings, or onsite working sessions.
Pacific and global time zone availability required.
Preferred Skills and Experience (As applicable - Specific skills, knowledge, and experience that are not required to perform the job, but are desirable to have)
Medical device, regulated industry, or global marketing organization experience preferred.
Experience establishing quarterly business reviews, operational health metrics, performance reporting, or ROI-informed creative operations reporting.
Experience mentoring team members, building readiness plans, and strengthening operational capability across cross-functional teams.

Primary Function of Position:
The New Product Verification Department is devoted to assuring safe, reliable, and effective products that exceed patient, surgeon, and hospital expectations. The department plays a vital role in product and process quality, in new product development and production, and in the quality of da Vinci and Ion robotic product lines, including diagnostic systems, endoscopic instrumentation, and supporting accessories. The engineering tech will work with a team of dedicated individuals within a product development team to assure the quality of new designs, to identify issues related to new designs and processes, and to work with other Test Engineers to develop harmonized test methods.
Roles & Responsibilities:
This position has responsibility and authority for:
Protocol Execution & Reporting
Executes test protocols for clinically-based surgical simulation and automated testing utilizing da Vinci Surgical Systems and other test equipment
Executes Design verification testing with guidance from the test owner
Identifies and reports problems that arise during testing, and escalates new or persistent failure modes to appropriate engineering teams
Provides documentation to the cognizant Test Engineer that clearly indicates the results of product testing
Follows GDP (Good Documentation Process) when filling out test data sheets
Performs instrument, endoscope and accessory cleaning and reprocessing
Generates work instructions for test methods or procedures.
Other Responsibilities
Ensures successful, on-time completion of department projects; communicates constraints to direct management when successful project completion is at risk
Performs a broad variety of tasks in support of product verification and test process design as assigned by department management
Complies with company Department and Standard Operating Procedures
Skills, Experience, Education, & Training:
Education and/or Experience:  High school diploma or GED, along with 2+ experience working in a hardware production or test environment. AS or BS degree in a scientific discipline is a plus.
Language Skills: Ability to read, write and understand English.  Ability to read and comprehend instructions, short correspondence, and memos.  Ability to write simple correspondence. Ability to effectively present information in one-on-one and small group situations to other employees, supervisors, or engineers.

Reasoning Ability:   Ability to apply commonsense understanding to carry out instructions.  Ability to report quality issues. Ability to suggest simple process improvements.  Must be a quick learner with the ability understand complex products and processes.
Computer skills:   Ability to use MS office tools- Word, Excel as part of daily work.  Ability to use on-line documentation. Ability to follow instructions to run software scripts.
Other skills and abilities:   Ability to work in a team environment. Ability to use basic tools and measuring equipment. Ability to work independently and with minimal supervision. Ability to multitask, and handle tasks with competing priorities effectively. Ability to work with biological samples, including blood, tissue and organs. Willingness to learn and contribute. Proactive and Self motivated.
Integrity: Accepting and adhering to high ethical, moral, and personal values in decisions, communications, actions, and when dealing with others

Relevant experience in a medical device company

The Learning Experience Research Intern is responsible for conducting external research, learner interviews, and competitive benchmarking to inform the future direction of Intuitive's customer learning programs. Analytical mindset with the ability to identify patterns, draw conclusions from qualitative and quantitative data, and formulate recommendations
Proficiency in MS Office (Word, PowerPoint, Excel)
Comfort engaging with external professionals (healthcare providers) in a professional, neutral interviewing capacity

Currently enrolled in a STEM field, Education, Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), UX Research, or a healthcare-related field (e.g. Health Informatics, or Biomedical Sciences) or related degree-seeking program at the Bachelor’s or Master’s level.

title: Manager System Analyst
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive. As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care, our technologies like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
Were a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
The Future Forward organization is Intuitive’s advanced concepts group. We explore emerging technologies, prototype next-generation solutions, and build software experiences that shape the future of robotic-assisted surgery.
If you're ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you'll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
Robotic Algorithms & Controls Engineers (Systems Analysts) at Intuitive Surgical play a critical role in developing the safest, highest-quality robotic platforms for minimally invasive surgery through rigorous engineering analysis, innovative problem-solving, and robust technical execution.
Systems Analysts are central to the design, development, integration, and lifecycle support of next-generation products across the da Vinci Surgical System portfolio. They are responsible for developing, optimizing, and validating algorithms that govern robotic manipulator motion, force control, and system safety across surgical robots, instruments, accessories, and endoscopes.
The role requires broad systems-level expertise and close collaboration across multiple engineering disciplines, including mechanical, software, controls, user interface, electrical, and safety engineering. Systems Analysts provide early technical input into product architecture and design decisions, rapidly evaluate and validate new concepts, and proactively address complex challenges in system integration, functional safety, motion and force control, and manufacturing.
Their ownership extends throughout the product development lifecycle, from early feasibility and architecture through design verification, system integration, manufacturing readiness, and commercial release. The ultimate objective is to deliver innovative robotic technologies that meet the highest standards of safety, quality, performance, and reliability for surgeons and patients.
The Manager of a Robotic Algorithms & Controls Engineering (Systems Analysis) team establishes responsibilities within their team. They are responsible for defining and meeting project milestones. They advise senior management on the technical strategy for product and platform projects. They work closely with other algorithms & controls, software, hardware, manufacturing, and clinical engineering teams to enable cohesion of design inputs, design architecture, specifications, and verification. They are expected to hire, coach, and retain Robotic Algorithms & Controls Engineering talent within their group
Essential Job Duties:
Manage and support a team of Robotic Algorithms & Controls Engineers towards successful accomplishment of product implementation with best-in-class solutions and architectures
Hire, retain key talent required for the team to be successful.
Provide in-depth analysis and characterization of electromechanical architectures during the entire design life cycle.
Facilitate mechanical, electrical, and software integration of new prototypes and new products including complete robotic systems, manipulators, instruments, accessories, and endoscopes
Analyze complex electro-mechanical devices for dynamic safety and clinical risk
Implement safety monitoring algorithms based on sound physics and risk analysis
Participate in clinical observations and experiments to ensure that performance requirements are relevant and realistic
Adhere to, and contribute to, design control processes, including design review presentations, design documentation, and verification & validation testing activities
Support the definition of manufacturing specifications and the ability to confirm devices meet those specifications
Document and pursue intellectual property
Communicate system architectural choices to the cross functional engineering team
Improve cross functional workflow and interaction through tool building and teaching others
Develop and own the tele-operated motion performance of robotic surgical instruments.
Ensuring motion fidelity will involve:
Working closely with the clinical development team to understand performance requirements;
Working closely with the mechanical design team to optimize the mechanism for motion fidelity;
Using analysis and experimentation to develop a deep understanding of the behavior and limitations of the instrument mechanism;
Modifying and tuning the algorithms to optimize motion fidelity and ensure consistent performance in the clinical environment.
Implement features and algorithms to support new instrument development, including collaboration with the design team to iterate through prototypes, analyze performance, and assess feasibility.
Perform risk analysis and implement safety algorithms. This includes documentation of risks, requirements, and test protocols to support requests for approval by regulatory agencies such as the FDA.
Analyze field data to continuously improve the performance and stability of the surgical instrument.
Collaborate with the manufacturing team to develop automated fixtures for calibrating, testing, and aiding assembly of the instrument. Additionally, determine manufacturing test specifications that will ensure instrument performance.
Lead by having a breadth of technical knowledge that enables a top-level view of the entire project. Using this perspective, you will act as an interface between various technical specialties.  Take ownership of issues that cross disciplinary boundaries and use your broad skillset to ensure the success of the project.
Required Skills and Experience
Exceptional embedded C/C++ programming capabilities as well as electromechanical and software integration skills.
Matlab programming capability
Familiarity with design control processes. Prior experience in product development under medical device standards (such as ISO 13485, IEC 60601, and IEC 62304), is a plus.
Demonstrate intuitive understanding of mechanical phenomena with ability to do rigorous mechanical analysis.
Knowledge of classical and modern servo control systems
Knowledge of serial-arm robot kinematics
Hardware, software, and mechanism integration skills
Intuitive understanding of mechanical phenomena with ability to do rigorous analysis.
Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal
Ability to work independently and the determination to solve challenging problems
Demonstrate ability to provide technical leadership and help define project tasks and objectives.
Required Education and Training
Minimum Masters in robotics related engineering field, with 6 years of experience in control of mechatronic systems, or Ph.D. with 3 years of experience in control of mechatronic systems.
Minimum 1-3 years of people management experience, or 3-5 years of cross-functional technical leadership in a Robotic Algorithms and Controls Engineers or equivalent role.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Prior knowledge of medical robotic and instrumentation control scheme
Knowledge of Python and basic SQL
Knowledge of statistics and probabilistic reasoning is plus
Knowledge of electrical, software, and mechanical design principles and CAD tools
Experience conducting research with human subjects
Experience launching real-world, commercially successful products

Primary Function of Position
The Staff Mechanical Design Engineer designs instrument and accessory products that enable surgery with the da Vinci system. They serve as a technical contributor and technical leader on projects across the product lifecycle, including early-stage feasibility (APD), new product development (NPD), and post-market sustaining engineering. The Staff Engineer identifies, develops, and refines technologies and product designs to address customer and business needs while supporting successful commercial launches and post-launch product improvements. The Staff Engineer consistently delivers high-quality technical output with significant impact across programs and product development efforts.
The Staff Mechanical Design Engineer leads significant technical workstreams and cross-functional product development efforts through strong technical execution, system-level problem solving and organizational influence. They independently solve complex engineering challenges, drive design decisions within their scope, and work closely with cross-functional partners to ensure alignment across technical, quality, manufacturing, supplier, and program requirements. This role requires broad mechanical engineering expertise, strong ownership, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced development environment. They operate with a high degree of autonomy, routinely making complex technical decisions, setting priorities, and influencing project direction across functions to ensure successful program execution. The Staff Engineer contributes to product development best practices and process improvements while helping ensure high-quality and reliable product outcomes.
The Staff Mechanical Design Engineer also supports the growth of the engineering organization by mentoring junior engineers, sharing technical knowledge, and modeling effective collaboration and communication behaviors across teams. The Staff Engineer is recognized as a trusted technical resource who improves team effectiveness through collaboration, mentorship, technical judgment, and strong communication across organizational interfaces.

Independently leads complex engineering activities from concept through implementation and applying broad expertise to deliver solutions across engineering and partner functions.
Solve challenging, multidisciplinary technical problems that require innovative thinking, system-level understanding, and collaboration across functions.
Drive high-impact technical decisions, establish priorities for self and project teams, and ensure alignment with overall program goals and business objectives.
Lead root cause investigations for difficult technical issues and orchestrates multidimensional cross-functional solutions while minimizing disruption to project timelines and deliverables.
Proactively identify project risks and drive cross-functional mitigation strategies. Influence technical tradeoffs, priorities, and execution plans across engineering and partner functions.
Develop and execute plans for large, complex projects involving multiple stakeholders and functions.
Influence technical strategy, engineering best practices, and process improvements within the business unit.
Provide technical leadership, mentorship, and coaching to engineers across the organization, accelerating individual development and overall team capability.
Review and assess the technical validity of design approaches, engineering analyses, and problem-solving methodologies across projects and teams.
Effectively communicate with stakeholders across all organizational levels, tailoring messaging to technical and non-technical audiences.
Build strong partnerships across functions and with external collaborators to drive successful project outcomes.
Creating intellectual property through the patent process, in collaboration with legal team.

Passion for solving complex technical problems with strong mechanical intuition, systems thinking, and persistence in driving issues to root cause using first principles engineering approaches.
Ability to operate with a high degree of autonomy while balancing technical excellence, business priorities, program timelines, and organizational objectives.
Ability to independently lead ambiguous and technically challenging work, rapidly learn new domains, and develop creative, practical solutions from evolving or incomplete requirements.
Ability to translate user and business needs into engineering requirements and solutions.
Strong expertise in experimental design, verification strategy, testing methodologies, data analysis, and statistical techniques including Design of Experiments (DoE) to support robust engineering decisions.
Recognized for sound engineering judgment and ability to evaluate, guide, and influence technical approaches across teams and disciplines.

Highly proficient in CAD-based design and documentation of complex mechanisms and systems.
Broad experience across all phases of the product development lifecycle, including concept development, feasibility, detailed design, implementation, debug, verification/validation, qualification, risk management, and design transfer to manufacturing.
Strong understanding of material selection, tolerance analysis, reliability engineering, and design for manufacturability (DFM/DFA) principles to enable scalable, high-quality products.
Extensive experience working with suppliers and manufacturing partners across a wide range of fabrication methods and processes, including multi-axis machining, MIM, plastic injection molding, overmolding, stamping, extrusions, additive manufacturing, laser cutting, and assembly processes.
Working knowledge of medical device development within regulated environments, including FDA QSR 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485, IEC 60601, and related standards and compliance requirements.
Strong technical communication and documentation skills, with the ability to tailor messaging effectively to technical teams, cross-functional stakeholders, leadership audiences, and external partners.
Ability to influence technical direction, drive alignment across organizations, and improve overall team effectiveness and engineering best practices.
Comfortable operating machine shop equipment and supporting hands-on prototyping, troubleshooting, and engineering development activities.
Ability to mentor and support the growth of less experienced engineers through technical guidance, coaching, and knowledge sharing.

Typically, at least 12 years of experience developing medical products or other relevant R&D experience (which may include graduate education).

M.S. or Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering or related field
Experience using SolidWorks strongly preferred

description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive. As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care, our technologies like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
Were a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
The Future Forward organization is Intuitive’s advanced concepts group. We explore emerging technologies, prototype next-generation solutions, and build software experiences that shape the future of robotic-assisted surgery.
If you're ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you'll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position:
As a Vision Software Staff Engineer, you will act as the technical lead for the software and embedded architecture definition of the real-time, high-definition video processing, imaging, and intra-body illumination systems at the heart of a new generation surgical robotic platform.
You will drive the deep integration of cameras, image sensors, and vision processing pipelines into complex, multi-processor embedded architectures, bringing sound engineering judgment to the trade-offs between hardware, software, and algorithms, and procedure-specific product requirements.
Critical to the success of this role is experience diagnosing and debugging complex vision systems end-to-end – from sensor and optics through the video pipeline to software – driving root cause investigations and collaborating with hardware and algorithms teams to resolve difficult, multi-disciplinary issues. Familiarity with working in a regulated industry and with design controls for medical devices is a plus.
The successful candidate must excel at evaluating design trade-offs through detailed technical deep dives, proof-of-concept development, and rapid iteration, translating rough requirements into robust, well-reasoned embedded software architectures.
A strong sense of shared responsibility and shared reward is required, as is the ability to make the work fun and interesting. Supporting you will be a development and management team that knows and cares about what you are doing and wants you to succeed.
Essential Job Duties
Lead the definition of hardware, software, and algorithms architecture for the real-time video processing engine, image sensors, and intra-body illumination systems of a new generation surgical robotic platform, from concept through implementation.
Drive the integration of cameras, image sensors, and vision processing pipelines into complex, multi-processor embedded architectures, ensuring robust interfaces between hardware, FPGA/ISP, and software components.
Evaluate multiple design trade-offs for the embedded vision software architecture through detailed technical deep dives, proof-of-concept development, and rapid iteration.
Lead bring-up and integration of new, high-performance cameras and image sensors, and the integration and evaluation of advanced camera pipeline video processing algorithms.
Diagnose and debug vision system issues end-to-end – sensor, optics, video pipeline, and software – leading root cause investigations in close collaboration with hardware, algorithms, and systems engineering teams.
Drive development and enhancement of the color and power control functions for intra-operative illumination.
Lead formal risk analyses for vision and illumination subsystems; identify additional hardware requirements and develop software mitigations to minimize potential failures.
Design and develop offline simulation environments and hardware/software diagnostic tools that accelerate development, debug, and test.
Perform and guide detailed design, development, documentation, and verification of embedded vision software and supervisory state machines, in compliance with regulatory requirements and Intuitive's internal guidelines.
Contribute broadly across the video and vision software stack, including extension of current processing frameworks to new hardware platforms.
Apply high-level and specialized imaging/vision expertise to deliver innovations and problem-solving approaches that can be leveraged across multiple products.
Mentor and guide engineers across the vision team.
Required Education and Training
Bachelor's degree or above in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a similar technical field.
A minimum of 12 years of experience developing and supporting embedded systems, with significant focus on video, imaging, or vision systems (or 8 years with a Master's degree, or 5 years with a PhD).

description:

A Systems Analyst is responsible for the detailed design and implementation of robotic control algorithms and safety systems for new surgical robots and instruments. This includes integrating and evaluating fully functional prototypes and conducting formal product testing.

Quick learning and a keen understanding of both user and engineering perspectives are essential,

Improve group workflow through tool building and robust cross-functional interactions.

Experience implementing, tuning, and debugging modern servo control systems.
Expert knowledge of robot modeling and system identification techniques.
Experience in designing and developing real-time control algorithms in C or C++, with the ability to assess numerical accuracy and computational complexity.
Working knowledge of Python or MATLAB/Simulink for control system simulation, analysis, and testing.
Excellent verbal and written communications skills, with the ability to communicate effectively across all levels of an organization.
Excitement to learn, solve tough technical problems, and to help improve patients' lives.

Expert in one or more advanced robotic control concepts such as impedance control or the control of flexible manipulators.
Experience designing software products in a regulated industry or for safety-critical applications; comfort with concepts of design input, design output, traceability, risk analysis, and mitigations.
Fluent working with software version control systems such as Git.
Working knowledge of embedded Linux or QNX at multiple levels including application, board bring-up, device drivers and distribution configuration.
Experience in all phases of the product development lifecycle including design, implementation, debug, verification, validation, and transfer to manufacturing.

title: Retail Sales Manager, Accelerator - BOSTON NORTH (MA)
description:
Job Description:
The Mars Retail Sales Manager is responsible for executing Mars Sales Strategy by applying fact-based selling techniques to influence customer decisions and achieve goals and objectives at Store Level.  Key responsibilities include delivering the Perfect Store, executing Account Headquarter plans, and delivering seasonal sell thru objectives and company priorities by identifying incremental selling opportunities for categories under your responsibility.
The primary role of the Retail Sales Manager (RSM) is to leverage data and insights to sell and execute company strategies and priorities by achieving Sales KPI objectives and creating best in class in-store conditions to engage consumers and drive consumption.  The expectation is that TSM will command strong knowledge of the category, shopper trends and consumer usage occasions enabling them to effectively sell incremental assortment and in-store solutions.
As an entry point into our MARS Sales organization, TSM is responsible for building strong customer relationships and collaborating across the Sales functions to identify and resolve operational issues.
The position requires a high degree of integrity with the ability to work efficiently and effectively in an independent fashion without direct supervision.  This position is field based within a defined geography and reports directly to a Retail Sales Lead.
Key Responsibilities
Build and maintain long-term, trusted relationships with customers by demonstrating strong consultative selling skills to drive sales, retailer profit, ROI, and market shar e.
Create value by delivering customized sales presentation(s) based on retailer opportunities and priorities to sell incremental orders and mutually beneficial in-store solutions.
Monitor and analyze performance metrics to identify and execute solutions to achieve territory and region KPIs, retailer category growth, and account/company business targets.
Leverage data and demonstrate a strong priority setting to deliver channel/retailer specific seasonal and limited time offer to sell through targets.
Serve as a primary point of contact for customers, ensuring clear communication of sales priorities, orders, and promotional plans.
Position yourself to be a trusted expert, asking open-ended questions and tailoring solutions to specific needs.
Influence merchandising and operational resources to ensure instore excellence, compliance with execution standards, and timely implementation of sales initiatives.  These include assortment priorities (core and innovation), shelving objectives and planogram integrity, as well as incremental semi-permanent and temporary displays.
Responsible and trusted use of technology is essential, including accurate data entry, analysis of sales data to build a selling story, and effective utilization of company systems to support decision-making and performance tracking.
May have Compression call responsibilities. Comfortable preparing and selling to Market Managers, District Mangers depending on customer base of your territory.
Direct 3rd party providers (where applicable) for in-store execution (including seasonal surge).
Where applicable, sell throughout the year by providing business updates to the store's decision maker and contracts which will support delivery of the distribution, shelving, and display objectives.  Enforce compliance.
Maintain high on shelf availability by working with KDM to address inventory discrepancies and order fulfillment.
Participate in team conference calls, training, and attend all sales meetings.
Responsible for storage facility and managing product rotation, inventory allocation, supplies, etc., in an efficient and effective way.
Job Specifications/Qualifications
Knowledge and Experience
Minimum Qualifications :
A bachelor’s degree, or HS Diploma and equivalent work experience
Demonstrated proficiency with intermediate technology tools, including mobile devices and basic business applications.
Strong analytical, problem solving, and negotiation skills.
Excellent interpersonal, communication, and relationship building capabilities.
Ability to lift and carry up to 40lbs
Able to sit, stand and/or drive for long periods of time, as well as frequently bend, kneel and stoop
Ability to walk for a minimum of 6 ½ hours per day
Demonstrate ability to work remotely
Subject to outside weather conditions and changing climates
Must live within territory boundaries
Ability to travel overnight if required
Work scheduled may include early mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays based on business needs.
Role requires daily travel to multiple customer locations and a valid driver’s license with a clean driving record.
Preferred Qualifications:
A bachelor’s degree and significant experience in field sales and territory management
2+ years with at least one year of selling experience
Proven ability to influence customers through professional selling skills and data driven insights.
Experience using technology to analyze performance, manage accounts, and support sales execution.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Work, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Power Bi.
Prior Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) and/or retail sales experience
Prior selling experience in convenience, grocery or Walmart channels.
What can you expect from Mars:
Work with diverse and talented Associates, all guided by the Five Principles.
Join a purpose driven company, where we’re striving to build the world we want tomorrow, today.
A strong focus on learning and development support from day one, including access to our in-house Mars University.
An industry competitive salary and benefits package, including company bonus.

title: Competitive Intelligence Lead
description:
About the Role

We’re looking for a Competitive Intelligence Lead, a senior individual contributor reporting to the Head of Competitive Intelligence, to help operationalize and scale the company’s competitive intelligence capability.

This person will own high-priority competitive analyses, executive-ready insights, and GTM enablement that help Product, Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and leadership understand where we win, where we’re vulnerable, and how the market is evolving.

This is not a traditional research role. It is a hands-on strategy role at the intersection of Product, GTM, Research, and Leadership. You will turn competitor movements, customer feedback, product data, and market signals into clear recommendations that influence roadmap decisions, positioning, pricing, sales execution, and executive decision-making.

What You'll Do 

 - Partner with the Head of Competitive Intelligence to translate the company’s CI strategy into repeatable analyses, operating rhythms, executive materials, and GTM enablement.

 - Own high-priority competitor deep dives, market landscape reviews, pricing analyses, product comparisons, Harvey Ball assessments, feature matrices, and strategic opportunity/risk assessments.

 - Create executive-ready insights that inform product strategy, roadmap prioritization, GTM planning, pricing, and investment decisions.

 - Develop best-in-class competitive messaging, objection handling, battlecards, and enablement content for Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Partnerships.

 - Monitor competitor product launches, model releases, acquisitions, partnerships, pricing changes, funding activity, customer announcements, and GTM motions.

 - Synthesize fast-moving and complex market information into clear implications, recommendations, and decision-ready narratives.

 - Partner closely with Product Management to identify areas of differentiation, competitive gaps, customer pain points, and emerging opportunities.

 - Collaborate with Marketing to sharpen positioning, messaging, and campaign strategy based on competitive dynamics.

 - Prepare executive-ready competitive briefs and contribute to board-level market and competitor analyses in partnership with the VP.

 - Help build and maintain dashboards, reporting, and knowledge repositories that make competitive movements visible and actionable across the company.

 - Develop frameworks that evaluate competitors across capabilities, enterprise readiness, developer experience, ecosystem, security, pricing, customer value, and strategic direction.

description:
About the Team

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.
This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

About the Team

OpenAI’s Education team works with K-12 districts, colleges and universities to bring AI into teaching, learning, research, and campus operations. We partner with the people who know those settings best, from faculty and teaching center staff to campus IT teams. Together, we help them choose where AI can be useful, learn how to evaluate its work, and build the expertise to teach others.



About the Role

As OpenAI’s first Enablement Lead dedicated to Education, you’ll shape how we help colleges and universities build that expertise. This is a hands-on, customer-facing individual contributor role. You’ll design the learning programs, teach the first cohorts yourself, and work with campus partners to lead future cohorts independently.



ChatGPT Edu will be central to your work. You might help faculty redesign an assignment around a specific learning objective, guide student developers through an OpenAI API or Codex lab, or help a campus IT team evaluate an AI-assisted workflow. You’ll work with institutional leaders to decide what success looks like and return after the session to see what people are using, adapting, and teaching their peers.



This role blends deep technical fluency, instructional design, and customer advisory. You will lead live trainings, workshops, and adoption interventions for audiences ranging from students, faculty members, staff, academic leaders and other relevant constituents, helping them understand not just what OpenAI’s products can do, but how to use them effectively in real-world contexts.

Success in this role means accelerating customer confidence and value, increasing product adoption, helping customers progress toward production use, and turning lessons from individual engagements into resources and practices that benefit many customers.



In this role, you will:

 - Own the learning plan for an institution from onboarding through broader adoption of OpenAI products, including ChatGPT Work, OpenAI APIs, Codex, Daybreak and other platform capabilities.

 - Work with Sales and Applied AI Architects to understand the institution’s goals, then identify who needs to learn what and where hands-on support will help.

 - Design and deliver high-impact training engagements, including onboarding sessions, advanced capability training sessions, executive briefings, hackathons, and hands-on workshops for audiences ranging from senior leaders to working teams.

 - Equip teaching centers, campus IT teams, and faculty or staff champions to teach others. Co-teach a session, give facilitators materials they can adapt, and use their experience leading the next cohort to improve the program.

 - Develop and refine reusable training assets, playbooks, and best practices based on patterns observed across customers and regions and scale them through OAI’s partner network.

 - Gather customer feedback from training and enablement engagements, synthesize themes across accounts, and relay insights to internal stakeholders to inform product and program improvements.



You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have 10+ years of experience owning an enterprise enablement or adoption initiative from discovery through results, aligning executive sponsors, business users, and technical teams around a measurable customer outcome.

 - Can build, test, and troubleshoot a working example using APIs or developer tools such as Codex. You can walk developers through how it works, explain how to evaluate the results, and help them adapt it to their own use case.

title: Geotechnical Engineer, Data Center Development
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Industrial Compute team is developing data center infrastructure to support increasingly demanding AI workloads. The team brings together site development, civil and structural engineering, utilities, construction, commissioning, and operations to move campuses from early evaluation through delivery.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Geotechnical Engineer to help evaluate, plan, and deliver data center campuses. You’ll translate subsurface conditions into practical recommendations for site selection, campus design, construction, and long-term reliability. The work spans early due diligence through design review and field execution, with a focus on identifying ground-related risks early and helping teams make informed decisions.

Key Responsibilities 

 - Develop, update, and maintain geotechnical and geoenvironmental scopes of work, Owner’s Project Requirements (OPRs), technical specifications, and engineering standards for site due diligence and design phases, ensuring consistency across data center and power infrastructure projects while supporting risk mitigation, cost optimization, and accelerated project deliver

 - Plan and review geotechnical investigations, including borings, in-situ testing, laboratory testing, and groundwater monitoring.

 - Evaluate subsurface conditions and develop recommendations for foundations, settlement, seismic design, earthwork, subgrades, pavements, retaining systems, slopes, and groundwater management.

 - Assess geotechnical risks during site selection and due diligence, including variable ground conditions, liquefaction, expansive or compressible soils, karst, settlement, and constructability constraints.

 - Review geotechnical reports, calculations, drawings, specifications, and consultant deliverables for technical quality and consistency with project requirements.

 - Partner with civil, structural, architectural, utilities, and construction teams to integrate geotechnical recommendations into campus plans and building designs.

 - Support permitting and agency coordination by providing clear technical documentation and responding to review comments.

 - Provide construction-phase support, including review of submittals and field conditions, evaluation of differing site conditions, and recommendations for corrective actions.

 - Help establish consistent geotechnical standards, investigation scopes, design criteria, and risk documentation across projects and sites.

 - Communicate ground-related risks, assumptions, and tradeoffs clearly to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

 - Review construction documents for foundation systems, earthwork, and ground improvement solutions for data center buildings, equipment yards, and power generation plants to ensure compliance with owner requirements, applicable codes, and project-specific geotechnical recommendations.

Qualifications

 - A degree in civil engineering, geological engineering, geotechnical engineering, or a related discipline.

 - Professional experience in geotechnical engineering for large, complex infrastructure, industrial, mission-critical, or campus-scale projects.

 - Strong technical judgment across subsurface investigation, foundation recommendations, earthwork, settlement, groundwater, and seismic considerations.

 - Experience reviewing consultant work and translating findings into actionable design and construction recommendations.

 - Familiarity with geotechnical analysis methods and common engineering tools used for foundation, slope, settlement, and earthwork evaluation.

 - The ability to work effectively with consultants, contractors, designers, and project teams while maintaining clear ownership of technical decisions.

 - Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain uncertainty and risk.

 - Experience supporting data centers, power generation, advanced manufacturing, or other critical infrastructure.

description:
About the Team

The Frontier Risks Safety team sets out safety requirements and executes planning for frontier model launches, including biological and cyber risks and government models. We work across research, engineering, and policy to assess risks, define and validate safeguards, and drive safety readiness throughout the model development and deployment process.  We also help shape frontier trusted-access programs, ensuring that access to advanced capabilities is supported by appropriate safeguards, clear requirements, and rigorous evaluation.

 

About the Role

As a Product Manager on the Frontier Risks Safety team, you will own product strategy, requirements, and delivery for initiatives that mitigate frontier AI risks and enable responsible access to advanced capabilities.  

You will partner with researchers, engineers, policy teams, and independent experts to identify the most important problems to solve, translate research and risk assessments into product requirements, and prioritize what to build.  You will guide work from discovery through deployment and iteration, making tradeoffs explicit and measuring whether the resulting safeguards and workflows address the risks they are intended to mitigate.

We’re looking for people who combine strong technical judgment, experience building and shipping complex technical products, and a commitment to AI safety. You should be comfortable working through uncertainty, engaging deeply with research, and adapting direction as capabilities, evidence, and user needs evolve.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

 

In this role, you will:

 - Set product strategy and priorities. Develop a shared understanding of frontier risks, deployment needs, and gaps in safeguards. Own the roadmap for mitigations, prioritizing investments based on risk, evidence, technical feasibility, and the value the underlying capabilities enable for users.

 - Drive frontier trusted-access programs. Ensure defenders and scientists have access to the frontier capabilities they need to strengthen security and accelerate scientific discovery.

 - Turn safety needs into product requirements. Work with model teams, safety researchers, engineers, and policy partners to translate threat models, evaluation findings, and user needs into clear requirements, acceptance criteria, and measurable outcomes.

 - Drive safeguards from concept to deployment. Partner with research and engineering teams to turn promising safety approaches into effective mitigations across models and products.  Resolve product and technical tradeoffs, manage dependencies, and drive delivery of improvements that close material safety gaps.

 - Own risk-area safety readiness. Own risk assessments and safeguard plans for launches in your area.  Define the requirements and evidence needed for readiness reviews with technical partners, surface unresolved risks early, and bring clear recommendations to accountable safety and deployment decision-makers.

 - Use evaluations to guide product decisions. Partner with researchers to prioritize capability evals, alignment and control assessments, adversarial testing, and safeguard stress-testing, including for autonomous and multi-agent systems.  Assess what the evidence establishes, where uncertainty remains, and how findings should change the roadmap.

 - Align teams and communicate decisions. Build alignment across research, engineering, product, and policy on goals, priorities, and tradeoffs.  Resolve blockers, establish clear ownership, and communicate results, limitations, and remaining risks through decision documents, launch reviews, and contributions to system cards and assessment reports.

 

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have 5+ years of product management experience, or equivalent experience owning the direction and delivery of complex technical products.

 - Have defined and shipped products or systems with researchers and engineers, particularly in AI, cybersecurity, biosafety, or another field where failures can have serious consequences.

 - Can turn ambiguous risks and user needs into a clear product strategy, prioritized roadmap, actionable requirements, and measurable outcomes.

 - Understand frontier AI safety concepts, including capability evals, alignment, control, monitoring, and safeguard robustness, and can engage substantively with technical teams.

4:00 pm- 2:30 am (Monday- Friday)
Overtime on Saturdays
Compensation

Join Our Team as a Finisher!
Are you passionate about metal finishing? S&C Electric Company is seeking a dynamic individual to coordinate our metal finishing function. As a finisher, you’ll be crucial in ensuring smooth operations and supporting our diverse team. The Finishing System is a process designed to pre-treat metal (i.e., powder coat and liquid paint) to protect it from the environment. You will work in a production environment, engage in continuous productive activity and must meet requirements within predetermined time constraints. Tasks require the use of both hands and arms on a repetitive basis for a full range of motion.

Identify parts from blueprints to verify that they are properly tagged.
Have the ability to use simple material handling equipment such as powered walking stackers, storage trucks and pallet trucks.
Use simple measuring equipment such as tape measures.
Have the ability to learn proper grinding procedures to smooth welds and remove scratches from steel parts and enclosures.
Hanging of parts weighing up to 200 lbs. on an overhead conveyor using material handling equipment.
Reacting to system alarms and basic sanding procedures.
The work in this area is physically demanding and requires the ability to sustain a continuous work pace for extended periods.
What you’ll Need To Succeed:
A working knowledge of shop math.
Ability to follow specific instructions and procedures.
Requirements:
High School Diploma
Physical demands:
Standing: All tasks are performed in a standing position with intermittent walking.
Lifting: Frequent lifting of items ranging in weight from 5 lbs. to 50 lbs.
Walking: Occasional walking moderate distances (less than 1/8 mile).
Carrying: Frequent carrying of items ranging in weight from 5 lbs. to 25 lbs.
Pushing: Occasional pushing of motorized material handling carts with loaded weights up to 1000 lbs.
Pulling: Occasional pulling of motorized material handling carts with loaded weights up to 1000 lbs.
Bending: Frequent bending and crouching to safely lift parts of various sizes and shapes.
Reaching: Continuous full range of motion from above the shoulders to below the knees.
Handling: Continuous handling of parts ranging in weight from 5 lbs. to 50 lbs.
Other: Respirator certification required.

Join Our Team as a Machinist!
Are you passionate about  Machining?  S&C Electric Company is seeking a dynamic individual to join our Metal Finishing Operations department. As a Machinist, you’ll be crucial in ensuring smooth operations and supporting our diverse team. You will be working in a production environment where all jobs have a measured standard production rate and you will be held accountable for the quality of your work. Most tasks require good hand/eye coordination and a full range of motion of both hands and arms on a regular and repetitive basis.
Key Responsibilities:
Responsible for operating automated and manual machines as part of a sheet metal processing cell. Machines include automated punching, forming, and laser cutting machines as well as manual and automated hydraulic press brakes. Operate various manual and CNC machines to fabricate parts in accordance with standard specifications.
Set up machines with the appropriate materials needed to complete the job.
Interpret blueprints, drawings, and other technical specifications to understand the requirements for basic parts and ensure accurate fabrication.
Perform basic routine maintenance on machines and tools to ensure longevity and quality fabrication, including cleaning and reporting mechanical/electrical issues to department leaders.
Utilize an overhead crane and other material handling equipment to safely position materials for machining.
Complete the first-piece inspection of parts using various measurement tools, confirming that the pieces are the correct material, quality, and specifications before beginning the machining process.
Maintain accurate records of fabrication activities, including tracking the progress of job orders and documenting corrective action needed for the machine, part, or process.
Meet department targets and consistently adhere to quality and safety standards.
Understand and comply with all applicable Company policies and rules.
Work with departmental mentors to gain and apply feedback in pursuit of improved work quality.
Maintain regular and punctual attendance.
Communicate effectively and respectfully with others.
Attend in-person or virtual meetings as requested or required.
Other responsibilities as assigned.
What you’ll Need To Succeed:
High School diploma / GED
Ability to use hand tools and precision measuring instruments such as tape measures and calipers.
Basic knowledge of machine controls and programs.
Ability to read blueprints.
Ability to work independently and meet requirements of assigned materials requests.
Good communication skills (written and verbal) with the ability to articulate information efficiently and effectively to team members in a variety of production support departments.
Basic computer skills with the ability to review and respond to requests via internal applications.
Basic math skills with the ability to calculate quantities, weights, and measurements.
Good interpersonal and organizational skills with the ability to understand and complete requests given by team members inside and outside of the department.
Ability and willingness to follow Health Safety & Environment procedures accurately, reporting concerns promptly to the safety action team.
Preferred:
1 year of machinist and manufacturing experience is a plus
Major Physical Demands:
Standing: Most tasks are performed in a standing position with intermittent walking.
Lifting: Frequent lifting of items ranging in weight from 5 lbs. to 50 lbs.
Walking: Occasional walking moderate distances
Carrying: Frequent carrying of items ranging in weight from 5 lbs. to 25 lbs.
Pushing: Occasional use of electric hand truck to move parts a moderate distance.
Pulling: Occasional use of electric hand truck to move parts a moderate distance.
Bending: Frequent bending and crouching required to perform a variety of tasks. Reaching
Reaching: Continuous full range of motion from above the shoulders to below the knees.
Handling: Continuous handling of parts ranging in weight from 5 lbs. to 50 lbs., along with a variety of hand-tools.
Other: Most tasks are performed in a standing position with intermittent walking.

Act as a subject matter expert for project management,  advising others on best practices.

4 + years of Project Management experience within a technical/engineering/manufacturing environment.
Excellent knowledge of and  demonstrated experience applying project management principles to manage a large portfolio of complex projects to successful delivery. Able to be tasked with the most challenging project assignments.
Sound technology  proficiency, including experience using project management tools such as Microsoft Project Professional.
Able to support mission-critical change management activities .
Leading project management skills  including the ability to create detailed project plans, define scope, establish timelines/milestones, and manage project finances and budgets at the highest level.
Excellent customer service orientation, ensuring satisfaction  of high-level customers and consistent communication throughout the most difficult projects.
Sound time management and organizational skills, coordinating internal and external resources, creative problem-solving when obstacles arise, prioritizing tasks, managing multiple  deadlines and keeping others organized.
Excellent interpersonal skills to  establish professional relationships built on mutual trust and respect, foster a shared sense of purpose in project teams, navigate and resolve conflict, moderate behaviors and foster collaborative working relationships across a diverse team and cross-functional project teams.
Excellent communication skills, (written, verbal, listening and presentation) able to liaise with internal and external stakeholders at all levels from leadership to support staff, and present influentially  regarding project progress and risks.
Business acumen,   critical thinking and analytical skills with the ability to use and analyze data to drive informed decisions, problem-solve difficult issues and leverage data and learnings to drive continuous improvement.
Financial acumen and numerical ability to manage project budgets and finances to maximum effectiveness.
Skilled at navigating through ambiguity, leading project teams through change and building change management into project plans.
Excellent presentation and facilitation skills to present project related updates, foster discussion  regarding project  plans and elicit contributions and discussion from stakeholders.
Agile project management approach with  an ability to help teams pivot approaches to meet project needs.
Preferred
Experience within the electrical power industry, with particular knowledge of medium and high voltage equipment and installation processes.
Experience in Lean Project Management implementation and transformation.
Experience with Jira, Confluence, or similar project management systems
If applicable as part of the GBS Program:
Experience working within a PMO or enterprise program environment, coordinating multiple concurrent initiatives.

Bachelor's degree in Project Management,  Technology, Engineering, a related field, or equivalent experience.
