Join Our Team as Vice President-Finance Operations!
Are you passionate about  Global Finance & Accounting?  S&C Electric Company is seeking a dynamic individual to join our Global Finance and Accounting team. As Vice President-Finance Operations,  you’ll be crucial in ensuring continued innovation and supporting our diverse team.
The Vice President - Finance Operations is responsible for leading the global finance organization supporting Production Operations and serving as the principal finance partner to Operations leadership. This executive role provides strategic financial leadership to optimize operational performance, drive profitable growth, improve productivity, and maximize return on capital investments across the manufacturing and operations network.
This role oversees financial planning, cost management, operational performance analysis, capital investment evaluation, and financial governance for Production Operations globally. Leveraging data-driven insights and strong business partnership, this leader identifies opportunities to enhance profitability, improve efficiency, optimize working capital, and support operational excellence initiatives.
The Vice President-Finance Operations reports directly to the Chief Financial Officer and works closely with the COO, Operations leadership, Value Stream leadership, Vice President of Accounting and Vice President of FP&A (Financial Planning & Analysis) to align financial strategies with business objectives, support enterprise decision-making and drive value creation across the organization.
Executive/Officer Obligations & Responsibilities:
Fiduciary Duty: Act in the best interests of the company and its shareholders by exercising care, loyalty and good faith in decision-making and prioritizing the company’s welfare over personal interests
Duty of Care: Make informed and reasonable decisions, considering all relevant information and acting with a level of care by conducting due diligence including conducting proper research, seeking expert advice and avoiding reckless decision-making
Duty of Loyalty: Avoid conflicts of interest and refrain from engaging in activities that could compromise the company’s interests, disclose any potential conflicts of interest, and ensure that personal interests do not interfere with the duty to the company
Financial Reporting: Deliver accurate and transparent financial reporting, providing shareholders and regulators with truthful and complete information about the company’s performance
Protection of Company Assets: Safeguard the company’s assets including intellectual property, physical property, and financial resources
Risk Management:  Identify and manage risks that could impact the company’s reputation or financial stability
Board Reporting: Interact with the company’s board of directors, providing them with information and updates on the company’s performance, strategy, and challenges.
Organizational Commitment: Demonstrate commitment to and be a champion for S&C’s Values and Guiding Principles of personal integrity, respect for people, commitment to excellence and responsible stewardship
Ethical Behavior: Lead by example and help team members understand and meet their ethics and compliance responsibilities as outlined in the Required Ethical Standards, Code of Business Conduct
Compliance with Laws and Regulations: Understand and ensure the company operates in compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, industry standards and company policies and drive decisions in line with the S&C signatory and delegation of authority
Health and Safety:  Champion S&C’s safety culture and uphold the duty of care to maintain a safe work environment in compliance with work health and safety regulations
Diversity, Equity and Inclusion: Promote and support an inclusive workplace culture that values diversity and embraces the principles of equal opportunity
Appropriate Workplace Behavior: Role model appropriate and professional workplace behaviors and play an active role in fostering a positive workplace culture at S&C
Continuous Improvement: Demonstrate a commitment to the ethos of continuous improvement and excellence through innovation
Personal Development: Drive personal development to continuously improve leadership skills through seeking feedback, engaging in self-development and being open to growth
Nothing in this Job Description is intended to limit an employee’s right to respond truthfully and fully to any question, inquiry or request for information when required by legal process, or from initiating communications directly with, or responding to any inquiry from, or providing truthful statements or testimony before, any self-regulatory organization or local, state or federal regulatory authority or administrative agency, regarding the employee’s employment with the Company, suspected or alleged unlawful practices or reporting possible violations of any law or regulation.
Essential Functions
Business Partnership and Support
Act as a strategic business partner to the COO and Operations leaders across the business, providing financial expertise and support to drive business initiatives.
Lead the Value Stream controllers in analytics, reporting and business support of the Value Stream leaders.
Lead the oversight of the company capital expenditure process, ensuring appropriate controls, analytics and cash forecasting across all functions.
Ensure accuracy of product margin data for business decision making.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to develop and evaluate business cases, investment proposals, and project financials.
Foster strong relationships with key stakeholders to ensure alignment of financial objectives with business goals.
Risk Management and Controls
Develop and implement effective risk management strategies to identify, assess, and mitigate financial risks, ensuring alignment with the enterprise internal controls framework and consistent standards for control design, ownership, execution, monitoring, and remediation.
Identify and implement operational finance tools to improve efficiency and insights.
Exercise sound business judgment and decision-making authority on matters with significant financial, operational, strategic, and organizational impact.
Champion the continuous enhancement of the company's internal controls framework, ensuring control effectiveness, regulatory compliance, and alignment with evolving business risks and operational objectives.
Direct the development, implementation, and governance of financial policies, controls, and operating procedures to drive consistency, compliance, and disciplined financial management across the organization.
Financial Reporting and Performance Management
Lead the development and maintenance of financial and operational performance indicators (KPIs), ensuring timely, accurate, and actionable insights that support performance transparency, decision-making and Value Stream objectives.
Provide Value Stream leadership with meaningful analysis of business performance, profitability, productivity, and operational trends to support informed decision-making and resource allocation.
Lead continuous improvement initiatives across finance and operations to enhance efficiency, strengthen financial performance, improve scalability, and support long-term growth.
Manage the capital expenditure process, ensuring appropriate ROI analyses, clear approval levels and required reporting.
Partner with Value Stream leaders and other Operations leaders to develop, implement and/or refine key operations initiatives, including resource planning, sales and operating planning, cycle counting programs and others.
People Management
Lead the Finance Operations organization, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and high performance aligned with company values and business objectives.
Build a sense of ownership and shared responsibility within the team, encourage employee feedback and involvement in team decisions, and address/mediate conflicts.
Lead, develop, and mentor finance leaders, building organizational capability and leadership bench strength to support current and future business needs.
Establish clear organizational goals, performance expectations, and accountability measures that drive business results and support strategic priorities.
Champion talent management strategies and processes for the team, including workforce planning, performance management, leadership development, succession planning, and employee engagement initiatives to ensure organizational effectiveness and long-term sustainability.
Foster an inclusive, high-performing culture that encourages innovation, collaboration, professional growth, and continuous learning across the organization.
Ensure the organization is appropriately structured, resourced, and aligned to meet evolving business objectives while driving operational excellence and financial performance.
Skills, Knowledge and Experience
REQUIRED
12+ years of experience in a senior finance position with experience in a manufacturing environment with an understanding of manufacturing processes and cost structures.
Superior strategic and financial acumen to forecast trends, create strategies and contingency plans to reach critical financial goals and business objectives, and lead finance-related transformation.
Financial planning capabilities to lead annual financial planning processes, model scenarios for future business and financial planning decisions, and support strategic business decisions.
Exemplary business acumen, entrepreneurial approach, and analytical skills with the ability to use and analyze data to drive informed decisions, problem-solve complex issues, and leverage data and learnings to drive continuous improvement and profitable growth.
Familiarity with Lean manufacturing principles and their financial impact.
Superior leadership skills, including the ability to lead leaders, guide, motivate, and delegate to deliver results, build teams and capabilities, embrace change, drive decisions and results, embrace culture and inclusion, and exhibit integrity.
Excellent communication skills, (written, verbal, listening and presentation) able to liaise with internal and external stakeholders at all levels from C-Suite to support staff, creative and persuasive in communicating and influencing outcomes, and able to successfully lead strategic planning discussions and present to a variety of audiences.
Demonstrated success coaching high-performing leadership teams that learn and apply complex, industry-specific concepts.
Exceptional interpersonal skills to establish meaningful relationships built on mutual trust and respect with stakeholders up to the C-Suite/Executive level, navigate and resolve conflict, moderate behaviors, and foster collaborative working relationships amongst a diverse audience.
Excellent organizational, planning, and project management skills, creatively problem-solving complex high-stakes issues and juggling a heavy volume of diverse strategic projects.
Expert-level Excel skills, including the use of formulas, pivot tables, sub-totals, linking spreadsheets, and conditional formatting.
PREFERRED
Experience with risk management and internal controls specific to a manufacturing environment.
Financial accounting abilities, including the ability to establish financial accounting controls and procedures, approve financial reporting structures, and develop financial accounting support systems.
Financial reporting abilities to build robust financial reporting frameworks and internal controls to secure the reliability of financial statements and compliance with procedures, laws, and regulations for financial reporting.

title: Implementation Consultant
location: Remote - CA; Remote - Chicago; Remote - Seattle; Remote - TX
description:
Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role:
Samsara’s Mid-Market Customer Success team advises and guides our customers, ensuring they adopt Samsara and continuously gain business value from our products. We are the trusted point of contact for Samsara’s Mid-Market customers throughout their lifecycle: onboarding, adoption, advocacy, and renewal.
In this role, you will be part of our Implementation team, responsible for helping Mid-Market customers deploy and adopt our IoT solutions for their fleet and industrial assets. Picking up where our sales teams leave off, you will own the customer relationship and ensure a successful deployment of Samsara's solution. Your customers span the entire range of businesses that power our economy, including trucking and transportation, food and beverage, passenger transit, utilities, school buses, and many others. All the while building relationships with the customer, helping them learn our system, establishing success metrics for business outcomes and overall ensuring a successful customer relationship.
Your role will be cross-functional in nature, working alongside and connecting Sales, Support, Sales Engineering, and Product, enabling you to experience multiple aspects of a fast-growing company from within.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Every phone call you answer and every email you send can affect whether truck drivers deliver goods on time and without accidents, whether students get dropped off safely from school, or whether power gets restored quickly after a natural disaster.
You thrive the most when solving problems: Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges for our Customer Success teams. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.
You are a natural relationship builder: Whether the relationship is with our customers or with cross-functional teams in Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team.
You are a Solution Architect at heart : You excel at explaining complex solutions, navigating intricate customer evaluations and deployments, and translating technical concepts into clear business value.
You are a Customer Advocate: You naturally analyze customer requirements, prioritize feature requests, and champion collaboration between customers and product teams to drive outcomes.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won't be your last at Samsara. This Customer Success team is still shaping its future and you will have plenty of autonomy and opportunities to master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals out there.
In this role, you will:
Be on the front-lines and ensure our customers increase the safety, efficiency, and sustainability of their operations with our IoT platform
Manage the deployment of Samsara technology to Mid-Market customers, enabling customers to achieve quick time to value in their investment
Create launch plans and a roadmap to increase product usage
Track implementation progress, participation, product adoption, and account health
Run training sessions, demonstrate Samsara’s technology, and work through challenges with executives and day-to-day users of the system across numerous use cases
Juggle multiple customer engagements in parallel and work cross-functionally to deliver an exceptional experience for our customers
Deeply understand the Samsara platform’s capabilities, explain them to customers of all types, and measure success of desired business outcomes
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices
Minimum requirements for the role:
3+ years of experience in an Implementation Consultant, Customer Success manager, account management, customer onboarding, or strategic consulting role. Mid-Market SaaS experience preferred
This is a demanding position with high internal visibility, that requires strong priority management and high emotional intelligence
Experience supporting or working with technical products
Excellent consultative skills with experience in end-to-end system implementations
Proven track record of building trust and communicating effectively with a wide variety of stakeholders: executives, Product and Engineering leadership, day-to-day users of our software
Experience defining business outcomes, measuring success through clear metrics and KPIs, and establishing ROI
Diplomacy, tact, and poise under pressure when working through customer issues
Bachelor’s degree from a 4-year institution
An ideal candidate also has:
Has strong bias for action, the ability to think big, with insistence on high standards
Has experience serving a large and complex customer base in B2B SaaS
Thrives in an unstructured, fast-paced, and change-heavy environment
Is well-versed in one of the following: cloud software, networking, automation, or control systems
Has experience with integration projects — at minimum, able to comprehend RESTful APIs; experience with scripting languages like Python is a plus
Has IoT, hardware, vehicles, or general tinkering experience (work or hobby) a plus
Has a background in Fleet, Logistics, Supply Chain, Telematics, Manufacturing, or general operations a plus
Is a resourceful self-starter who proactively troubleshoots and solves problems independently
Has practical experience using AI tools to build reports, automate tasks, or improve daily efficiency

title: Manufacturing Quality Inspector
description:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots. Full-stack robots—hardware, software, and AI—all designed and assembled in Glen Cove, New York. The company makes AI-native robots anyone can buy and deploy, with customers ranging from family-owned machine shops to the Fortune 500. Customers include Sunoco, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the U.S. Army, along with hundreds of manufacturers nationwide. Standard Bots raised a $200 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation from RoboStrategy, General Catalyst, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and Samsung Next.


About the role

Robots only work if every part is exactly what it claims to be — and you're the one who makes sure of it. You'll be the final word on mechanical quality in our QC lab, using GD&T to catch what others miss and confirming that the parts going into our robots match the drawings they came from. Get it right, and every arm we ship starts on solid ground.


What you'll do

- Inspect mechanical parts and assemblies in the QC lab using GD&T (ASME Y14.5), catching deviations before they turn into downstream problems.

- Program and run CMMs and other advanced measurement equipment to verify parts against spec.

- Lead First Article Inspections for mechanical parts at launch and after any process change.

- Run process audits on production mechanical operations so quality holds steady as we scale.

- Mentor Receiving Inspectors on mechanical inspection techniques and GD&T fundamentals.

- Keep inspection records and traceability tight and audit-ready for all mechanical work.

- Take a seat on the Material Review Board and help resolve mechanical nonconformances.

- Review mechanical drawings for inspectability, and flag GD&T issues to NPI and Engineering before they cause rework.

- Support our 6S and FOD programs to keep the QC lab clean, organized, and safe.


What you'll bring

- 5+ years of mechanical inspection experience in a QC lab environment.

- Strong working knowledge of GD&T per ASME Y14.5.

- Hands-on skill with measurement equipment — CMM preferred, plus height gauges, optical comparators, and surface plates.

- Sharp drawing interpretation skills.

- The patience and precision to work through complex measurements without cutting corners.


Nice to have

- CMM programming experience with PC-DMIS, Calypso, or similar software.

- Experience inspecting industrial robotics or precision mechanical assemblies.


Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this role is $34-40/hour, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

We believe in creating a warm and welcoming space where every cup of coffee sparks connection.   As a coffeehouse leader, you don’t just run a business—you lead a team that creates moments of connection and joy.    Every day provides an opportunity to lead with craft and heart, making your coffeehouse a place where your community feels welcome.

We'd love to hear from people with:

Legal documentation establishing your identity and eligibility to be legally employed in the country in which you apply.

Join us and connect with something bigger, apply today!
As a Starbucks partner, you (and your family) will have access to medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, and other voluntary insurance benefits. Partners have access to short-term and long-term disability, paid parental leave, family expansion reimbursement, paid vacation from date of hire*, sick time (accrued at 1 hour for every 25 hours worked), eight paid holidays, and two personal days per year. This list is subject to change depending on collective bargaining in locations where partners have a certified bargaining representative. For additional information regarding partner perks and more detailed information about benefits, go to starbucksbenefits.com .

title: technical product manager principal - (Edge Foundation Services)ST, Seattle, WA
location: 2401 Utah Ave S #800, Seattle, Washington, United States
description:
Now Brewing – Edge Foundation Services Leaders! #tobeapartner
From the beginning, Starbucks set out to be a different kind of company. One that not only celebrated coffee and the rich tradition, but that also brought a feeling of connection. We are known for developing extraordinary leaders who share this passion and are guided by their service to others.
Edge Foundation Services builds the full-stack platform powering Starbucks stores worldwide (soon). Our work spans edge compute, deployment, device management, networking, and the operational capabilities that keep technology reliable across company-operated, licensed, and franchise locations. As a Principal Technical Product Manager, you’ll shape the product direction for this ecosystem; building relationships across the larger Starbucks organization, understanding how technology is implemented across teams, and bridging product needs with engineering concerns to deliver secure, resilient platforms that make every store easier to evolve.
You’ll partner with the teams that depend on our foundational services, turning thousands of coffeehouses into a consistent, scalable runtime and giving product teams a paved path to deliver new experiences with greater speed and confidence. Working across engineering, product, architecture, security, and operations, you’ll build trusted relationships, uncover technical dependencies and constraints, align roadmaps, and translate between business priorities and engineering realities. You’ll also help shape how AI moves from experimentation to safe, reliable production in stores, ensuring the right capabilities and guardrails exist for store partners and customers.
As a Principal Technical Product Manager you will…
Own the product vision from edge to experience  Define the product strategy and roadmap for edge platform capabilities, connecting customer and store-partner needs with engineering delivery and operations.
Build relationships across Starbucks  Partner with leaders and teams across the larger organization to understand their goals, build trust, create alignment, and make Edge Foundation Services the platform of choice.
Bridge product needs and engineering concerns  Understand how technology is implemented across teams, translate technical complexity into clear priorities and trade-offs, and bring engineers, architects, and product partners together around the right solution.

title: Senior Facilities Engineer - Straddle Projects
location: United States of America - Colorado - Denver
description:
Job Family Group:
Engineering Group
Job Description:
bpx energy, a major oil and gas producer in the United States, leverages its expertise in unconventional gas, including shale, to deliver hydrocarbon production and technical knowledge worldwide. With operations in Texas and Louisiana, our US onshore business has become both a premier oil and gas producer and a leader in reducing methane emissions.
As part of BP, a global industry leader, we foster a high-energy, high-intensity environment built on accountability, collegiality, innovation, and empowerment. At bpx, we support our people to learn and grow in a diverse and challenging environment where collaboration, continuous improvement, and inclusion are valued.
Discover your place with us and help our business meet the challenges of reimagining and reinventing the future of energy.
Role Synopsis
Lead the engineering development and execution readiness of Eagle Ford Straddle projects. Owns projects from Project Development handoff through engineering completion and handoff to the Program Manager for execution. Ensure projects have a complete engineering design, construction work package, MOC documentation, and Operations alignment before construction begins.
Key Accountabilities
Engineering owner for all Eagle Ford Straddle projects. Responsible for developing executable project scopes, managing third-party engineering contractors, coordinating Operations and Maintenance input, and delivering construction-ready work packages that support safe, cost-effective project execution.
Program Ownership & Optimization
Own Straddle projects from Project Development handoff through Program Manager handoff.
Develop project scope, engineering basis, design packages, and construction-ready deliverables.
Apply consistent engineering standards, lessons learned, and best practices across Straddle program.
Identify and mitigate engineering, constructability, operational, and execution risks early in project
Vendor Relationships & Performance Management
Lead the third-party engineering contractor through the engineering phase of each Straddle project.
Define engineering deliverables, expectations, review cycles, and quality requirements.
Coordinate development of engineering drawings, construction work packs, material takeoffs, tie-in packages, P&IDs, plot plans, electrical and instrumentation details, and other project-specific deliverables as required.
Review contractor deliverables for technical quality, completeness, constructability, and alignment with BPX expectations.
Drive timely resolution of engineering questions, design issues, scope gaps, and field conflicts.
Hold the engineering contractor accountable for quality, responsiveness, and schedule performance.
Engineering and Construction Work Pack Development
Develop complete engineering and construction work packages.
Coordinate constructability reviews with Construction, Operations, and Maintenance teams.
Ensure packages include scope definition, tie-in requirements, isolation plans, material requirements, and execution considerations.
Identify long-lead materials, critical path items, and execution constraints.
Budget Forecasting & Cost Management
Forecast annual program budgets - bottom-up by equipment count, rate, and duration
Track actuals vs. forecast monthly; identify and explain variances
Provide budget inputs to Program Engineering TL for total spend reporting
Identify cost reduction opportunities within each program without compromising performance
Operations and Maintenance Engagement
Engage Operations and Maintenance throughout project development.
Lead field walkthroughs and design reviews.
Incorporate field feedback into project designs and construction packages.
Ensure projects support safe operation, maintainability, and long-term reliability.
Management of Change Ownership
Create and steward Management of Change documentation for each Straddle project.
Ensure MOCs accurately capture the project scope, technical basis, affected equipment, operating impact, safety considerations, documentation updates, and required approvals.
Coordinate with Operations, Engineering, Maintenance, Construction, HSE, and other stakeholders to complete required MOC reviews.
Track MOC progress and ensure required documentation is complete before project execution.
Confirm that drawings, operating procedures, equipment records, and other controlled documents are updated as required through the MOC process.
Ensure MOC documentation is structured consistently across all Eagle Ford Straddle projects.
Project Development to Execution Handoff
Deliver complete handoff packages to the Program Manager for execution.
Clearly communicate project scope, risks, assumptions, material requirements, and key decisions.
Support project execution by resolving engineering questions and design clarifications.
Capture lessons learned and incorporate improvements into future projects.
Scope, Cost, and Schedule Support
Support project estimating, AFE development, and execution planning.
Identify cost, schedule, and constructability risks.
Drive standardization opportunities that improve execution efficiency and reduce cost.
Essential Experience and Education
Bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering, Petroleum Engineering, Mechanical Engineering
7+ years of engineering experience supporting upstream oil and gas production facilities, midstream facilities, or comparable process facilities.
Demonstrated experience serving as a Project Engineer or Facilities Engineer responsible for developing projects from early scope definition through construction-ready design.
Strong brownfield facility modification experience, including tie-ins, equipment additions, piping modifications, instrumentation, electrical/controls interfaces, and integration with operating facilities.
Experience developing and reviewing P&IDs, plot plans, equipment specifications, piping plans, tie-in packages, material takeoffs, construction work packs, and other engineering deliverables.
Experience leading HAZOP/PHA, constructability, design, MOC, PSSR, and project-readiness reviews for operating facilities.
Experience leading and managing third-party engineering contractors, including defining scope, reviewing deliverables, managing technical comments, resolving design issues, and maintaining engineering schedules.
Demonstrated ability to coordinate engineering across multiple disciplines, including mechanical, piping, civil/structural, electrical, instrumentation, controls, and automation.
Experience working directly with Operations, Maintenance, Construction, HSE, Automation, and other engineering disciplines during project development.
Hands-on experience with Management of Change (MOC) processes for modifications to operating facilities.
Experience conducting field walkthroughs, constructability reviews, design reviews, and project readiness reviews.
Experience identifying long-lead materials, tie-in constraints, operational impacts, constructability issues, and execution risks before construction.
Working experience with project estimating, AFE development, forecasting, cost tracking, procurement support, and schedule development.
Experience supporting projects by resolving RFIs, field conflicts, design clarifications, and scope changes.
Desirable Criteria
Direct experience developing and executing brownfield compression projects, including compressor installations, inlet separation, suction and discharge piping, coolers, control valves, measurement, instrumentation, electrical systems, and facility controls.
Experience taking projects through the full engineering lifecycle, from initial field walk and scope development through detailed engineering, MOC, procurement, construction-ready work packs, execution support, commissioning, and startup.
Demonstrated experience acting as the owner's engineer while managing third-party EPC or engineering contractors, including establishing deliverables, reviewing engineering quality, challenging designs, controlling scope, and driving schedule performance.
